382YE Spring Equinox Imperial elections.d: New or returning senators were chosen for Segura, Reikos, Holberg, Mournwold, Karsk, Spiral and Temeschwar. Spiral's seat was allocated to Urizen in the Senate, and Temeschwar's senator resigned after the last session. The Ambassadors to Faraden and the Commonwealth both died in the Sunday battle, as did the new holder of the Scorrero Nets. Marciel i Riqueza took the Fire of the South after Gomez i Souza i Guerra's death. Theoderic Ulfarsson took the Fist of the Mountains after Axehind of Dunhearth Hall was revoked. Synod and Conclave posts were filled. The Grandmaster of the Rod and Shield died, and Bourse seats and titles were sold or voted.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but Spiral, which it held that season, had its Senate seat allocated to Urizen.
n.Highguard: Cadeus of the Shattered Tower kept the Senate seat for Reikos, and Zephaniah of Highguard remained Grandmaster of the Sevenfold Path.
n.The Brass Coast: Avisena i Kharizmi i Guerra was returned as Senator for Segura for 5.5 thrones. Marciel i Riqueza became General of the Fire of the South after the death of Gomez i Souza i Guerra.
n.The League: Caerwyn von Holberg won Holberg's Senate seat and Temeschwar's senator resigned. Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg became General of the Quiet Step using Defender of the Empire, and the League senators appoint the Steward of the Sarvos Mana Exchange.
n.The Marches: Robert Dunlain was returned as Senator for Mournwold.
n.Urizen: The Senate allocated Spiral's seat to Urizen, and Tanwyn Ankarien became Senator for Spiral.
n.Varushka: Maarit was returned as Senator for Karsk.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Kai Dunning of Wintermark resigned as Master Apothecary.

t.Holberg: Caerwyn von Holberg of the Feasting Crow was elected Senator for Holberg.
t.Karsk: The incumbent Maarit kept the Senate seat for Karsk.
t.Mournwold: The incumbent Robert Dunlain kept the Senate seat for Mournwold.
t.Reikos: Cadeus of the Shattered Tower, the incumbent, remained Senator for Reikos.
t.Segura: Avisena i Kharizmi i Guerra kept the Senate seat for Segura at a price of 5.5 thrones.
t.Spiral: Spiral's Senate seat was allocated to Urizen, and Tanwyn Ankarien became its senator.
t.Temeschwar: Giuseppe Sanguineo is listed as Senator for Temeschwar, and the page records that the senator resigned after the last Senate session.

382YE Spring Equinox Senate sessions.d: The Civil Service put the Imperial treasury at 1514 thrones and 4 crowns, and Imperatrix Lisabetta used the Hand of the Chancellor for 504 thrones and 4 crowns. The Senate appointed ambassadors to Faraden, Otkodov and Sumaah, and allocated Brilliant Shore, the Legacy and the Singing Caves. It also passed a law prohibiting Bite, created a Roll of Benefactors, abrogated the Bursar of the Academy and approved many commissions, among them a seminary in Reikos and the Golden Causeway. Motions to improve the House of Barbs and to increase the Grandmasters' stipend failed. The Imperial Guerdon went to the Wolves of War, the Fire of the South, the Bloodcloaks and the Tusks.

n.Highguard: The Senate passed a motion to raise a Highborn army and approved the construction of a seminary in Reikos, which Highguard held.

t.Reikos: The Senate approved the construction of a seminary in Reikos, and the Arcane Architect announced an intention to build a summer vis sinecure there.

382YE Spring Equinox winds of fortune.d: Zenith fell to the Druj, prompting rumours of a long-dead Throne's return. At the Ambassador's invitation, five thousand Suranni troops from Kalino crushed rebel slave camps in Feroz. The Zemress exiles settled in Segura. A curse settled over Therunin, while the Navarr checked the vallorn in Liathaven. Orc peace talks drew delegations, the bay was mapped, and Murit and Soghter transformed into a new eternal. Seven Synod mandates were upheld, including Severin von Holberg's sermon against religious conflict and the consecration of the Silent Sentinel. The Mournwold remained stable as fortifications began. The Blood Cloaks army was completed, and the Winter Sun became Freedom Fighters.

n.Dawn: A Dawn Assembly mandate celebrating the defence of Semmerholm gave every herb garden in Dawn bonus production for the season, and Lady Caewyn may submit a song to improve it. Dawn was also tagged in the orc peace talks and the magical round-up.
n.Druj: The Druj took Zenith amid eerie events and rumours of a dead Throne's return, while the Trade Winds discussed the imminent threat of a Druj invasion.
n.Grendel: Grendel menaced the city of Siroc in Madruga and dominated the Bay of Catazar, complicating Imperial sailing; the cats of Spiral also featured in the magical round-up.
n.Highguard: People unexpectedly emerged from a forest in northern Highguard, and the Synod consecrated the Silent Sentinel in Casinea as a site of pilgrimage.
n.Imperial Orcs: Bloodcrow Losak was sent with liao to preach the Way to the former Jotun thralls of the Mournwold, and the nation permanently changed the Winter Sun's quality to Freedom Fighters.
n.Jotun: Jotun delegations joined talk of peace treaties, and the Empire opened dialogue with the former Jotun thralls in the Mournwold, who were declared foreigners by the Senate.
n.Navarr: The Navarr stymied the vallorn's expansion in Liathaven, opening a rare chance to drive it back, while a troubling curse settled over Therunin.
n.The Brass Coast: The Zemress exiles settled in Segura and Suranni troops crushed rebel slave camps in Feroz. Grendel also threatened Siroc in Madruga, and Varushkan armies now suffer penalties when fighting alongside the Brass Coast.
n.The League: The bite trade fuelled a crisis on the streets of the four cities, Lorenzo la Volpe's growing legend divided opinion, and Severin von Holberg delivered an Empire-wide sermon on virtue.
n.The Marches: Sister Meredith was sent to preach the Way to the Mournwold orc thralls, fortifications began in Greensward and Freemoor, and Sarcombe was granted a charter should it be rebuilt.
n.Thule: Thule was one of three orc nations involved in the season's talk of peace treaties with the Empire.
n.Urizen: A new runeforge in Redoubt featured in the magical round-up, and Urizen was tagged in the Trade Winds' international developments.
n.Varushka: Following Bogdan Bogdanovich's mandate, all Varushkan armies suffer penalties for fighting alongside Wintermark and the Brass Coast, and their generals have choices to make about army qualities. Commissions following the epic storm in Varushka remain available.
n.Wintermark: The Blood Cloaks army was completed, giving Wintermark three armies. A rare Sentinel Gate conjunction opened to Kallavesa, and Kalpaheim weighed the opportunities of the Blood Red Roads.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Senate-commissioned mapping of the bay went ahead, amid the challenges facing sailors on Grendel-dominated waters.
t.Casinea: The Silent Sentinel was consecrated in the name of Vigilance, making fortifications easier to build and allowing a place of pilgrimage to be built.
t.Feroz: Five thousand Suranni troops crossed into Feroz and smashed the rebel slave camps along the border, executing most of the rebels or returning them to the Iron Confederacy in chains.
t.Hahnmark: Kalpaheim, Wintermark's "city", examined the opportunities offered by the Blood Red Roads' easy access to the whole Empire.
t.Holberg: As one of the League's four cities, Holberg faced the bite-trade crisis threatening their street life, as well as the constructions tied to Lorenzo la Volpe's growing legend.
t.Kalino: The Suranni Duke of Kalino sent five thousand troops into Feroz at the invitation of the Imperial Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy.
t.Kallavesa: An exceptionally rare Sentinel Gate conjunction led to the marshes of Kallavesa, signalling an opportunity for Winterfolk heroes.
t.Liathaven: Navarr efforts stymied the vallorn's spread, leaving its forces overextended and offering a once-in-a-generation chance to drive it back.
t.Madruga: The Grendel threat to Siroc, the city of sails, was a matter of great concern.
t.Mournwold: The territory remained stable as fortifications began, Sarcombe received a charter, and priests began bringing the Way to the former Jotun thralls. Everyone waited to see what would happen with the Singing Caves.
t.Redoubt: A new runeforge in Redoubt was among the season's magical developments.
t.Segura: The Zemress exiles settled here and were eager to reshape their new home, though integrating them proved far from straightforward.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the magical round-up included something about the cats of Spiral.
t.Therunin: A highly problematic curse settled over vallorn-haunted Therunin.
t.Zenith: Zenith fell to the Druj, followed by eerie unexplained events and rumours of the imminent return of a long-dead Throne.

r.Liathaven/Liath's Heart: The vallorn's forces coiled in the depths of Liath's Heart were overextended and weakened, presenting an opportunity to strike against them.
r.Mournwold/Freemoor: Work began on fortifications in Freemoor.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Work began on fortifications in Greensward.

382YE Spring Equinox winds of war.d: The Druj abandoned Semmerholm to Dawn's armies, aided by Varushkans and Summer knights, then overran Zenith, killing over 1,500 Highborn and destroying the Gardens of Pallas. Marcher armies drove the remaining Grendel raiders from Lightsea and most of Free Landing, though Atalaya held. Navarr and Marchers repelled the vallorn in West Ranging, losing nearly 1,500 soldiers, opening a chance to strike into Westwood. About eighteen thousand Jotun took Stark and half of Tanikipari. In Spiral, Imperial armies took Ankra, Ossuary, Screed and the Legacy, destroying three Grendel armies, but the Iron Helms' terror magic woke the Black Plateau, imposing heavy ongoing penalties. Eight Sentinel Gate conjunctions were identified for the Spring Equinox.

n.Dawn: Dawn's four armies, joined by Summer knights their witches summoned from Eleonaris, liberated all of Semmerholm without a major battle as the Druj withdrew; Dawnish magic also sent two further cohorts of knights to fight in Spiral.
n.Druj: The Druj quit Semmerholm for the Barrens but poured some thirty thousand orcs into Zenith, seizing the whole territory, beginning to turn Proceris into marsh and slaughtering prisoners where the Halls of Knowledge once stood.
n.Grendel: The Grendel abandoned most of Madruga with their plunder, keeping Atalaya and a few small islands, but in Spiral they lost Ankra, Ossuary, Screed and the Legacy, and three whole armies—the Salt Dogs, Sand Pipers and Stone Gyre—were destroyed.
n.Highguard: The Granite Pillar, Valiant Pegasus and Seventh Wave were driven out of Zenith, losing more than fifteen hundred Highborn while covering the Urizeni evacuation, before rallying at Cargo in Limus.
n.Jotun: Some eighteen thousand Jotun under the Queen in the North's champion invaded Sermersuaq, taking Stark and half of Tanikipari with unusual caution, while their raiders lingered in West Marsh and an envoy apparently went to the Thule.
n.Navarr: The Quiet Step, wielding the flame of Surut, led the campaign that turned back the vallorn in West Ranging, while the battered Black Thorns withdrew from Madruga to Miaren.
n.The Brass Coast: Madruga was largely freed of the Grendel with the help of Freeborn corsairs, though priceless relics from Atalaya's museums were carried off, and the Red Wind Corsairs raided profitably in Spiral and showed restraint amid the madness.
n.The League: The Towerjacks returned from furlough in Sarvos to fight in Spiral, where under the Black Plateau's influence they came to echo some of the Iron Helms' atrocities.
n.The Marches: The Drakes and Strong Reeds liberated Lightsea and most of Free Landing, while the Tusks and Bounders fought the vallorn in West Ranging, where some eight hundred yeomen fell and were denied burial in their homeland's soil.
n.Thule: Wintermark scouts reported a Jotun group received by the Thule in the Silver Peaks foothills, raising fears of an alliance, though the Thule took no part in the invasion.
n.Urizen: Urizen lost Zenith entirely, along with Spire Calator and the Gardens of Pallas, and its refugees fled to Morrow and Redoubt; Spiral is now Imperial, but the Citadel Guard remains at risk of disbanding unless another region of Spiral is taken.
n.Varushka: The Golden Axe helped Dawn clear Semmerholm, while the Iron Helms' cabalists unleashed a terror in the night on the Grendel in Spiral that broke them but woke the Black Plateau, killing or driving mad the cabalists themselves.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark faced a Jotun invasion of Sermersuaq that took Stark and half of Tanikipari with little resistance, and feared further Jotun moves into West Marsh in Kallavesa and a Jotun pact with the Thule.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step, Tusks and Bounders marched south out of Bregasland's marshes to fight the vallorn in West Ranging.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks' general urged them to charge 'like heroes of Holberg'.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the defeated Navarr Black Thorns marched north through Kahraman on their way to Miaren.
t.Kallavesa: Jotun warriors still haunt northern West Marsh, close to the newly conquered Stark, and their raiding parties are gathering there, perhaps to tighten their hold on the region.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: the Iron Helms' cabalists drew on the darkness beneath the hills of Karov for their ritual in Spiral.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: the Iron Helms' cabalists drew on the darkness beneath the hills of Karsk for their ritual in Spiral.
t.Liathaven: The vallorn's push into West Ranging was turned back at heavy cost, leaving the Empire building a beachhead in the north-west and a rare chance to strike at the vallorn in Westwood, though vast swathes of forest were burned.
t.Madruga: Marcher armies retook Lightsea and most of Free Landing almost unopposed, but Atalaya and a few small islands remain in Grendel hands, and much of the territory's wealth was carried off.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: the battered Black Thorns withdrew toward the safety of Miaren.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: the Iron Helms' cabalists drew on the shadows beneath the trees of Miekarova for their ritual in Spiral.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold is not named on the page and is linked only through the Marcher armies' wider campaigning.
t.Morrow: Urizeni refugees fleeing Zenith were evacuated to Morrow, and displaced Zenith Urizen were offered new holdings there.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes' general declared the Mournwold won, and the Marcher armies marched down out of the Mourn into Madruga as the Navarr passed through northwards.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: a Jotun group was believed to be an envoy to the Thule orcs of Otkodov.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt took in refugees from Zenith, and the three Highborn armies rallied at Cargo in Limus, now dangerously close to the Druj front.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: retreating Highborn recalled the earlier loss of Haros Water and Riverwatch to the same Druj foe.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks returned to Spiral from their furlough in Sarvos.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm is once again entirely in Dawnish hands after the Druj withdrew, burning manors and villages and leaving raiders who were hunted down or driven into hiding.
t.Sermersuaq: The Jotun conquered Stark and half of Tanikipari, sending thralls west, and their raiders and scouts ranged across the territory while defenders were overwhelmed hall by hall.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: Winterfolk who chose thraldom were sent west to Skallahn.
t.Spiral: The Empire now controls Spiral and may assign it through the Senate, but the awakened Black Plateau brings heavier casualties, no natural resupply, reduced production and doubled upkeep at the Legacy.
t.The Barrens: The Druj armies retreated back into the Barrens toward Dawnguard, and a Sentinel Gate conjunction offered a chance to strike at Lerrovac's Camp in Murderdale.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: Winterfolk who chose thraldom were sent west to Tromsa.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: the Iron Helms' cabalists drew on the shadows beneath the trees of Volodmartz for their ritual in Spiral.
t.Zenith: Zenith fell entirely to the Druj, who destroyed spires and the Gardens of Pallas and began turning Proceris into marsh; only a handful of spires shielded by Night magic remain protected.

r.Bregasland/North Fens: Mentioned in passing: yeomen raised among the rushes of North Fens leapt at the chance to cross by boat to the islands of Free Landing.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: Jotun raiders still haunt northern West Marsh and were gathering at a Summer regio on the Westerhal Trail, where a Sentinel Gate conjunction offered the Empire a chance to strike.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: The vallorn was prevented from seizing West Ranging, but the Empire holds only a partial beachhead; fire and Surut's immolation destroyed most of its Spring regio and stripped the region of its forested quality.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: Ettercaps emerged from Westwood during the fighting, and the weakened vallorn left an opportunity to push into the region and possibly cleanse it, though casualties would be high.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Most islands of Free Landing were liberated, putting the Empire eight-tenths of the way to control, but Atalaya and a few smaller islands remain occupied and its museums were looted.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: The Marchers drove south along the Lightsea coast and retook the region, routing raiders at Quzar within hours.
r.Redoubt/Limus: The three Highborn armies rallied at Cargo in Limus, where a quarter of Zenith's population had gathered as refugees, now perilously near the Druj front.
r.Reikos/Haros Water: Mentioned in passing: Highborn recalled the earlier fall of Haros Water to the Druj.
r.Reikos/Riverwatch: Mentioned in passing: Highborn recalled the earlier fall of Riverwatch to the Druj.
r.Semmerholm/Axmure: The Druj forces that had fallen back into Axmure withdrew south without a fight, and Dawn's armies camped and feasted with their Summer allies beneath its trees.
r.Semmerholm/Ulvenholm: The orc bandit bands that had long harassed Ulvenholm left south with the Druj, to the relief of the yeofolk and Navarr there.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: Two Sentinel Gate conjunctions open into East Floes near the site of the Winter Solstice battles against the drowned dead.
r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: The Jarl of Aftanes' warband probed into Sealtoq in an apparent feint and was repulsed by the Suaq, though many Suaq fell.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Steinr wardens reported a Jotun group passing into the Silver Peaks foothills to be received by the Thule.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: Stark fell quickly to the Jotun, who are now dug in there, using the village of Rest as their base and relighting the Sentinel's Rest beacon as a great bonfire.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: Mentioned in passing: it is unknown whether Jotun scouts have learned of the new mine in Suaq Fount.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: The Jotun are halfway to controlling Tanikipari after taking the Hot Springs of Taniki, and a large Jotun force resting at the Spring Hills is a Sentinel Gate target.
r.Spiral/Ankra: Four Imperial armies crushed the Grendel in Ankra and liberated the region.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: The season's final battle was fought at Solen's Doubt on Apstrus, where the Black Plateau woke; the Empire withdrew, leaving the Grendel in control.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Retreating Grendel regrouped at Apulus, which remains in their hands along with the southern coast.
r.Spiral/Cinion: The Imperial Orc armies reinforced the assault on Ankra from Cinion, which, with Ankra, Ossuary and Screed, now gives the Empire Spiral.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: After a two-week siege the Empire took Ossuary and recaptured the Legacy mithril mine, which may be allocated at the Spring Equinox but now has doubled upkeep.
r.Spiral/Screed: The Iron Helms took Screed with savage cruelty and unleashed their terror ritual there, and a Sentinel Gate conjunction reaches the Gethern Expanse, where elite Grendel mercenaries are heading.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: The Druj armies leaving Semmerholm crossed back into the Barrens toward Dawnguard.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: A Sentinel Gate conjunction leads to Lerrovac's Camp in Murderdale, where Imperial prisoners are held by a powerful Druj Tepel and a major orc force.
r.Zenith/Clypion: The Druj flooded Clypion, felling spire after spire and slaughtering prisoners at the empty site of the Halls of Knowledge.
r.Zenith/Iteri: The Highborn made their last stand in Iteri, losing hundreds at the Utique fords as Spire Calator and the Gardens of Pallas were burned.
r.Zenith/Proceris: The Druj overran the Highborn foothold in Proceris and, with miasma pillars, are turning it into marshland, giving it the marsh quality.

A bit of peace.d: About a dozen Jotun, led by the old Jarl Ustigar with the Hierro orcs Kenza and Juevar, travelled openly to Anvil as guests of Liissá of Sigehold, bound for a meeting with Avisena i Kharizmi i Guerra. Rak Who-Speaks-For-The-Dragons-United would return to negotiate before the Thule peace treaty ended, refusing to discuss surrendering the Silver Peaks or Krevsaty. He complained that Thule archaeologists had been ordered out of Hercynia and that a Navarr deal over Sküld was imperilled. The Great Forest orcs, still settling Therunin, planned an informal visit bearing gifts. With unnamed allies, they and briar humans freed Dawnish prisoners from the Barrens and led them through Peytaht to Reikos.

n.Druj: Dawnish captives escaped from a Druj labour camp in the Barrens, and the Druj did not follow them into the Great Forest of Peytaht. The freed prisoners told harrowing tales of Druj cruelty and back-breaking work under malicious overseers.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Reikos took in more than a hundred and fifty freed Dawnish captives at Remember Exile. The senator for Reikos was to receive gifts from the Great Forest orcs in thanks for herbs provided to them.
n.Jotun: Having invaded Sermersuaq, the Jotun sent a delegation of about a dozen under a flag of truce to Anvil, led by Jarl Ustigar with the Hierro orcs Kenza and Juevar. They came as guests of Liissá of Sigehold to meet the Jarl of the Golden People.
n.Navarr: Rak said the Dragons were disappointed that Thule archaeologists had been told to leave Hercynia, which imperilled an agreement allowing the Navarr to dance the Dance of Navarr and Thorn in Sküld. He urged the Navarr to send a good-faith negotiator, naming Merel. Meanwhile the Navarr in Therunin were learning to live alongside the Great Forest orcs.
n.Thule: Rak Who-Speaks-For-The-Dragons-United was to return to Anvil to seek a new treaty before the existing one ended at the Summer Solstice. The Dragons refused to discuss giving up the Silver Peaks or Krevsaty, and had recalled their archaeologists from Hercynia.
n.Wintermark: Winterfolk watchers in Hahnmark let the Jotun truce delegation pass unmolested, honouring the law protecting delegations. This was despite the Jotun having invaded Sermersuaq.

t.Casinea: The Thule declared that Krevsaty, ancestral land returned to them under the earlier treaty, was not up for negotiation. Any Imperial demand that they quit it would end the talks in failure.
t.Hahnmark: The Jotun delegation walked openly south through Hahnmark under a flag of truce. Its Winterfolk watchers chose to let them pass and report to their Thane.
t.Hercynia: At the Empire's request, all Thule visitors to Hercynia were recalled to Otkodov. They had believed they had leave to recover culturally significant items there.
t.Otkodov: The Dragons of Otkodov sent Rak back to Anvil to continue peace negotiations. They expressed disappointment at the revoked Hercynia agreement.
t.Reikos: Over a hundred and fifty freed Dawnish yeofolk and some nobles arrived at Remember Exile in Reikos, escorted by Great Forest orcs and briar humans. Its senator was due to receive Great Forest gifts at Anvil.
t.Sermersuaq: The Jotun had invaded Sermersuaq, and their truce delegation set out south from there. The Thule insisted they would not give up the Silver Peaks.
t.The Barrens: Dawnish captives were liberated from a Druj labour camp in the Barrens during the Winter Solstice and led away through Peytaht.
t.Therunin: The Great Forest orcs continued settling in Therunin alongside the Navarr, settling occasional problems by arbitration. Their work on the Holt of the Oak was slow for lack of weirwood and money, and about two dozen freed yeofolk went back with them.

r.Hahnmark/Southridge: From a tower in Southridge, a Winterfolk captain stopped a young warrior from shooting at the passing Jotun envoys. She upheld the law and the spirit of truce.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: The Dragons' agreement to let the Navarr perform the Dance of Navarr and Thorn in a suitable regio in Sküld was left severely imperilled.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The Thule declared the Silver Peaks ancestral land that they would not surrender. They warned that any demand to quit them would wreck the negotiations.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: More than a hundred and fifty yeofolk and a handful of nobles from the houses of Dawnguard were freed from Druj captivity. Most hoped to rejoin their houses-in-exile.

Allocate the Singing Caves Spring 382YE.d: In Spring 382YE the Senate considered a motion to allocate the Singing Caves, a mithril mine in the Mournwold. The senator for Bregasland proposed it and the senator for Astolat seconded it. The motion passed, making the Singing Caves a Marcher national Bourse position rather than one open to the whole Empire. The position was to be filled at the Summer Solstice by Marcher citizens who own farms.

n.The Marches: The Singing Caves became a Marcher national position, to be appointed by Marcher farm-owners at the Summer Solstice, putting control of a mithril mine in Marcher hands.

t.Mournwold: The Singing Caves mithril mine in the Mournwold was formally allocated as a national Bourse position, to be filled at the Summer Solstice.

Appoint Ambassador to Otkodov Spring 382.d: The motion to appoint a new Ambassador to Otkodov was proposed by the senator for Karsk and seconded by the senator for Karov. It passed, and the resulting election was held at the Sunday afternoon session of the Senate. Yvengi Katzev was appointed Ambassador to Otkodov.

n.Thule: Thule, which held Otkodov at the time, saw the Senate appoint Yvengi Katzev as the Empire's Ambassador to Otkodov.

t.Otkodov: Otkodov gained a newly appointed Imperial ambassador, Yvengi Katzev, while the territory was held by Thule.

Archive:382YE Spring Equinox Imperial ti.d: Empress Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg also used the Throne's power of Defender of the Empire to command Navarr's League of the Quiet Step. The Senate seat for Temeschwar was vacant, as were several ambassadorships, the Dean of the Academy and the Imperial Master of Works. Spiral's senator, Tanwyn Ankarien, was still listed among Urizen's senators. The Synod's cardinals came from Dawn, Wintermark, the League, the Imperial Orcs and elsewhere. The Archmagi and Grandmasters were recorded, as were the Bourse seats and the prices paid for them. The Thule were recorded as holding Wintermark's Stonefield Ice Caves. Three Imperial wayleaves auctioned at the Winter Solstice were also listed.

n.Dawn: Dawn held Senate seats for Astolat, Semmerholm and Weirwater and fielded four generals, including Tancred and Garravaine de Rondell. Viviane de Coeurdefer and Abaddon De Rondell sat as Cardinals of Ambition and Wisdom.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, though Spiral, which it held, still appeared with a senator listed among Urizen's.
n.Highguard: Highguard held four Senate seats, Bastion, Casinea, Necropolis and Reikos, and three generals, including Brother Lucifer of the Valiant Pegasus. Its citizens filled numerous Synod and Conclave posts.
n.Imperial Orcs: Irontide Vio represented Skarsind, and Bloodcrow Morg'ur and Irontide Skar led the Winter Sun and Summer Storm. Atla sat as Cardinal of the Way and Chainbreaker Snark served as Chaplain Consular.
n.Navarr: Navarr held seats for Hercynia, Miaren and Therunin, and Eira Pridestalker commanded the Black Thorns. The Empress herself took command of the League of the Quiet Step as Defender of the Empire, and Heilyn of Bronwen's Rest served as Warmage.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast filled all four of its Senate seats and fielded two generals, Estana i Mestiere i Guerra and Marciel i Riqueza. Esteban i Del Rio Blanco i Guerra served as Imperial Fleet Master.
n.The League: A Leaguer, Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg, sat on the Throne. The League held seats for Holberg, Sarvos and Tassato, but Temeschwar's seat was vacant, and Astrid Fjellrevening Rezia di Tassato and Irada von Temeschwar sat as Cardinals of Pride and Vigilance.
n.The Marches: The Marches filled all four Senate seats and fielded four generals, among them Marius Woodville-Talbot and Black Jack. Marchers also held the posts of Conscience of the Senate and Imperial Inquisitor.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are recorded as holding Wintermark's Stonefield Ice Caves Bourse position.
n.Urizen: Urizen's senators were listed for Morrow, Redoubt and Spiral, and Nicassia Avicia of Phoenix Reach commanded the Citadel Guard. Urizeni also served as High Exorcist and Seer of the Gateway.
n.Varushka: Varushka held all four of its Senate seats and three generals, including Akstis Eigulys of the Northern Eagle. Irina Akulinovna Kotor served as High Bard of the Empire.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark held seats for Hahnmark, Kallavesa and Sermersuaq and fielded three generals, including Lofyn Bloodcloak. Jorma Steelhail and Veikko were Cardinals of Courage and Loyalty, though the Thule were recorded as holding the Stonefield Ice Caves.

t.Astolat: Bohemond de Rondell served as Senator for Astolat.
t.Bastion: Sammual, of the Cohort of the Winter Bear, served as Senator for Bastion.
t.Bregasland: Orrick Bolholt served as Senator for Bregasland, the Dour Fens.
t.Casinea: Nira, of Cantiarch's Hold, served as Senator for Casinea.
t.Feroz: Chiara i Zayden i Riqueza served as Senator for Feroz.
t.Hahnmark: Hengest Dun served as Senator for Hahnmark.
t.Hercynia: Rhisiart Dancewalker served as Senator for Hercynia.
t.Holberg: Caerwyn von Holberg of the Feasting Crow served as Senator for Holberg, the home of the reigning Empress.
t.Kahraman: Qusay i Kalamar i Guerra served as Senator for Kahraman.
t.Kallavesa: Edythe Dunne served as Senator for Kallavesa.
t.Karov: Pipski Bearonovitch Strascovich of the Vor'azi served as Senator for Karov.
t.Karsk: Maarit served as Senator for Karsk.
t.Madruga: Adan i Del-Toro i Riquezza served as Senator for Madruga.
t.Miaren: Llewellyn Leafstalker served as Senator for Miaren, and Tanwen Snowstep held the sinecure of Eternal Flame of Miaren.
t.Miekarova: Father Nikolovich Drakov served as Senator for Miekarova.
t.Mitwold: William Guildenstern served as Senator for Mitwold, Pride of the Marches.
t.Morrow: Ariadne of Auric Horizon served as Senator for Morrow.
t.Mournwold: Robert Dunlain served as Senator for Mournwold, the Mourn.
t.Necropolis: Jeconiah, of Raven's Watch, served as Senator for Necropolis.
t.Redoubt: Andronikos served as Senator for Redoubt.
t.Reikos: Cadeus, of the Shattered Tower, served as Senator for Reikos. Issachar held the Great Forest at Reikos Bourse seat for 200 Thrones.
t.Sarvos: Magdelena Alagna di Sarvos served as Senator for Sarvos. The ministry of Steward of the Sarvos Mana Exchange stood vacant.
t.Segura: Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra served as Senator for Segura.
t.Semmerholm: Lady Ailliena Devereux served as Senator for Semmerholm.
t.Sermersuaq: Atte served as Senator for Sermersuaq.
t.Skarsind: Irontide Vio served as Senator for Skarsind. The sinecure of Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting was vacant.
t.Spiral: Although Spiral was held by Grendel, Tanwyn Ankarien was still listed as its senator among Urizen's. Maryc was recorded as Castellan of Spiral Castle.
t.Tassato: Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato served as Senator for Tassato, and Edwin Sanguineo di Tassato held the ministry of Steward of the Tassato Mana Exchange.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar's Senate seat stood vacant at this Equinox.
t.Therunin: Cybi Farkas served as Senator for Therunin.
t.Upwold: Henry Ward served as Senator for Upwold, the Silver Chase.
t.Volodmartz: Alexei Volostra served as Senator for Volodmartz.
t.Weirwater: Lady Eve Orzel served as Senator for Weirwater, and Rada held the Weirwater Vales Bourse seat for 280 Thrones.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Mentioned in passing: the Great Pits of Ennerlund Bourse seat was held by Vasiliy Krenyenkov Valeskai Strascovich for 370 Thrones.

Assignment of Spiral Spring 382YE.d: The motion, proposed by the senator for Redoubt and seconded by the senator for Segura, simply resolved that Spiral be assigned to Urizen. It passed. As a result, Spiral became a Urizen territory and went on to elect a senator, giving it representation in the Senate once more. The page records only the assignment and the election of a senator, not who held the territory on the ground.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named in the motion; the map records Grendel as holding Spiral that season, while the Senate assigned the territory to Urizen.
n.Urizen: Urizen formally gained Spiral as one of its territories, and with it a new Senate seat, since Spiral went on to elect a senator.

t.Spiral: Spiral was assigned to Urizen by the Senate and elected a senator, restoring its representation in the Senate even though the map records it as held by Grendel that season.

Before the sunrise.d: A magnitude fifty Spring curse, apparently Rivers of Life, infused Therunin's waters with healing power, but threatened to stir its vallorn; the counter-ritual Rivers Run Red is interdicted. The Suaq Qimmiq Swiftblade and Nukilik Adamantine, who attacked the Krampus, agreed to face inquisition at Anvil. The Spiral Sword runeforge was finished near Cargo in Redoubt, with its Seer title to be auctioned through the Bourse. Irra Harah offered boons for the hearts of Zadkiel de Coeurdefer, Chiara i Zayden i Riqueza and Henry Ward. Stars stayed hidden over Semmerholm and the Barrens and vanished over Zenith, strengthening naga secrecy. Penumbral veils covered Urdur, Necropolis and Redoubt, and the Sussivari Frost Coven raised the Citadel of Fog in the Morass.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish naga Zadkiel de Coeurdefer had a bounty placed on his heart by Irra Harah, and the stars remained hidden over Dawn's territory of Semmerholm, impeding scrying and heightening naga secretiveness there.
n.Druj: The stars remained absent over the Druj-held Barrens and vanished over Druj-occupied Zenith, whose proximity left the new runeforge vulnerable to any Druj move against Redoubt.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but cats in Spiral, which Grendel partly held, suffered a Night curse of nightmares.
n.Highguard: A ritual shroud warped the stars over Necropolis and shielded it from scrying, bringing heavy dark fog, while the runeforge stood on the road to the Highborn trading-port of Hedra.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Krampus-beast linked to Skarsind was attacked and slain at the Winter Solstice, though its spirit was reportedly banished to the Krampushall in Pakaanan's Pass and reformed there.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun advance into Liathaven thirty years ago was recalled as a time when using Rivers of Life near a vallorn was cautioned against, and Liathaven's vallorn remained a source of uncertainty.
n.Navarr: Rivers of Life settled over Navarr Therunin, healing wounds but thickening the vallorn's miasma and making giant insects restive, with attacks on isolated steadings reported.
n.The League: The Sussivari Frost Coven again raised a misty fortress in Holberg's Morass, and masked strangers in its fogs sometimes aided hunters and travellers against orc ambushes.
n.The Marches: Henry Ward of Upwold was one of three citizens whose hearts Irra Harah sought, and Thomas of Upwold was among the benefactors who funded the Spiral Sword.
n.Thule: Thule appeared to have drawn the penumbral veil over Urdur in Otkodov, filling its night sky with strange phenomena; whether Nithoggir, Sküld or Verthandi were similarly veiled was unclear.
n.Urizen: The Spiral Sword runeforge was completed in Redoubt, which was also shrouded against scrying, and Spiral's cats were tormented by a Night curse, prompting two magicians to leave for Redoubt.
n.Wintermark: Many Winterfolk were troubled by the assault on the Krampus, and the stormcrow Baena Stormsdottir, injured in a fall, urged other Wintermark priests to inquisit the Suaq perpetrators Qimmiq Swiftblade and Nukilik Adamantine at Anvil.

t.Holberg: The Citadel of Fog rose again in the Morass, its mists spreading across the territory with masked figures who sometimes helped travellers, before dissipating shortly before the Equinox.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: questions over the active status of Liathaven's vallorn added to fears about Therunin, and its stars were among those missing during 381YE.
t.Necropolis: A ritual shroud warped Necropolis's stars, protected it from scrying for the coming year and brought heavy, dark fog.
t.Otkodov: Urdur appeared to be under a Thule penumbral veil, with misplaced constellations and eerie lights; whether other regions were veiled was uncertain.
t.Redoubt: The Spiral Sword runeforge was completed on the road between Cargo and Hedra, dangerously close to Zenith, and a shroud now hid Redoubt from scrying behind warped stars and dark fog.
t.Semmerholm: The stars remained absent over Semmerholm under a magnitude fifty Night shroud, impeding scrying and strengthening naga secretiveness.
t.Skarsind: The Krampus-beast associated with Skarsind was attacked at the Winter Solstice, its spirit reportedly reforming in the Krampushall.
t.Spiral: Every cat in Spiral suffered a Night curse of nightmares for three months, and many residents' cats went missing, apparently having fled.
t.The Barrens: The stars remained hidden over the Barrens, impeding scrying and heightening naga secrecy, with the shroud expected to last until shortly before the Winter Solstice 382YE.
t.Therunin: Rivers of Life infused all of Therunin's waters with healing magic, but risked stirring its vallorn, with miasma thickening and giant insects attacking isolated steadings.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Henry Ward of Upwold was targeted by Irra Harah's bounty and Thomas of Upwold helped fund the runeforge.
t.Verthandi: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether the penumbral veil over Urdur also covered Verthandi.
t.Zenith: The stars vanished over Druj-occupied Zenith shortly before the Spring Equinox, and its nearness to Redoubt left the new runeforge exposed.

r.Holberg/The Morass: The Sussivari Frost Coven's dripping castle of mud, reeds and roots rose again from the Morass, wreathed in vision-limiting mists.
r.Necropolis/Hedrossan: Mentioned in passing: Hedrossan is not named, though the runeforge's road leads to the Highborn port of Hedra and Necropolis as a whole was shrouded.
r.Otkodov/Nithoggir: Mentioned in passing: it was unknown whether the penumbral veil over Urdur also lay over Nithoggir.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: Mentioned in passing: it was unknown whether the penumbral veil over Urdur also lay over Sküld.
r.Otkodov/Urdur: Merchants at Thule trading posts in Urdur reported misplaced constellations, a randomly shifting moon and eerie lights, suggesting a penumbral veil.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: The Krampus's spirit was reportedly banished to the Krampushall in Pakaanan's Pass and reformed there, though its return to full strength was uncertain.
r.Spiral/Screed: Mentioned in passing: the curse on Spiral's cats seemed unconnected to the thing in Screed.
r.Therunin/Greenheart: Stories told of the vallorn miasma thickening in Greenheart as the Spring curse took hold.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: Stories told of the vallorn miasma thickening in Sweetglades as the Spring curse took hold.

Beg, steal, or borrow.d: Jules i Conzara i Guerra, a Siroc trader acting for the Asavean Lord Magnus Tullis, sought relics of paragons and exemplars and asked to meet the Cardinal of Prosperity. Oswald the Red, a battlefield looter enriched by the Grendel rout in Spiral, offered mostly artisan magic items plus one supposedly Eternal artefact. Lani of the Red Hills coven sought authentication of a letter about a lost tomb linked to the divining crystal of Riqueza. Loud Pat of Beech Hill brought a Feni letter to fund repairs after a raid. A survivor of burnt Torvaldshall brought a jar said to hold a spirit. Two Navarr of Fabledwing Striding called a meeting of bestiary compilers.

n.Grendel: Following their crushing defeat in Spiral, Grendel dead and fallen have been widely looted, and many of their magic items are now being sold on, including by Oswald the Red at Anvil.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named, though the summit visitors gather at Anvil in Casinea.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Kallavesi hunters in the accompanying fiction briefly suspect the Jotun before finding the Torvaldshall survivors.
n.Navarr: Two Navarr of Fabledwing Striding arranged a Friday evening meeting in the Forge for bestiary compilers, zoologists and veterans of beast-hunting to share knowledge and plan future hunts, rescues and studies.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn feature prominently: Jules i Conzara i Guerra came to buy relics for an Asavean lord, and Lani of the Red Hills coven brought a letter tied to the fabled divining crystal of Riqueza, with a possible auction if it proves authentic.
n.The Marches: Beech Hill's alder Matt of Redston sent Loud Pat to Anvil with a captured Feni letter, hoping to sell its news to alders, beaters and other Marchers to fund repairs after the Feni raid.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: a Kallavesi warrior in the fiction compares the looting in Spiral to fighting alongside the Thule.
n.Wintermark: Torvaldshall, a small mostly Suaq hall, burned down and one survivor travelled to Anvil to sell a haunted jar, while the looter Oswald the Red planned to seek out fellow 'maggots' in the Wintermark camp, a term many Winterfolk despise.

t.Casinea: Anvil in Casinea drew all these sellers and petitioners for the Spring Equinox summit, with meetings arranged at the Forge and the Anvil Library.
t.Hahnmark: Torvaldshall, a hall on the border of Hahnmark and Kallavesa, burned to the ground and its survivors took to the floes to hunt.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: the Fabledwing fiction recalls a successful hunt of vallorn-infested Mandowla near Twr Uchel and Bont Goch, with help from the Pride of Hercynia.
t.Kahraman: Lani's antique letter was found in a rotting attic on a Kahraman goat farm the Red Hills coven once visited.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the relic-buyer Jules i Conzara i Guerra is a trader from Siroc.
t.Spiral: After the Grendel defeat in Spiral, the plain below Solen's Doubt became an open graveyard drawing looters from many armies, and some looted items appear to be Urizeni, with murkier legal standing.
t.Upwold: A Feni band extending its raids southwards has troubled households throughout eastern Upwold, prompting Beech Hill to seek funds and sell information about them at Anvil.

r.Upwold/Ashbrook: The market town of Beech Hill in Ashbrook was raided by Feni, leaving its people mostly unharmed but its property wrecked, goods stolen and its reputation as a safe trading town damaged.

Benevolence, inspiration, and legacy.d: The General Assembly upheld Severin von Holberg's mandate (886–232), which sent him with liao to remind citizens of their shared belief in the virtues. His sermon argued that Benevolence, Inspiration and Legacy are the signs that should guide everyday action. Its effect is that attempts to stir religious conflict are strongly inhibited for a year, muting outrage over the Suranni enslaving rebels in Feroz, the Iron Helms' deadly strike in Spiral, the Zemress Islanders, the Yaelites and the Asavean Architect. In response, moderates under Teodora Bezavina proposed stripping the National Assemblies of statements of principle, while radicals under Bishop Orlando di Holberg proposed abolishing them. Scholars suggested cutting the paragon signs to three, which reopened debates about miracles, exemplars and the Sumaah.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named; the page refers only to the Iron Helms' strike on the Black Plateau in Spiral, which Grendel held that season.
n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly's rejection of Yael is noted, and a Highborn movement is pressing to undo Atuman's demotion. The radicals' plan would also change Highguard's senators to be chosen by its priests rather than a National Assembly.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the nation's founding is cited as a Legacy, and Bloodcrow Ergot's statement urging the orcs to ignore some ancestors is given as a potential source of division that the sermon helped suppress.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn shock at the Suranni enslaving rebels in Feroz and anger at the deaths caused by the Iron Helms have been kept from erupting by the sermon. Religious differences with the Zemress Islanders have also been set aside for now, though hostility to Varushka endures.
n.The League: The League's Severin von Holberg, Bishop of Ambition, authored the mandate and sermon. Bishop Orlando di Holberg of the University of Holberg leads the radicals calling for the National Assemblies to be disbanded.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the sermon reached congregations in Sarcombe, and the Mournwold slaughter is said to remain fresh in people's minds.
n.Varushka: Western anger at the Iron Helms' brutal tactics has been stifled, so no one is openly denouncing Varushka, but the Coast and Wintermark remain hostile, and that hostility now seems set to endure. Varushkans also feature in the debate: Teodora Bezavina of Delev speaks for the moderates and Vera Runova Helgrod faces the Sumaah question.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark remains openly hostile to the Varushkans after rejecting their cruel ways, though the sermon has kept that hostility from becoming active agitation. The sermon was also preached in Gildenheim.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: some theologians argue that true followers of the Way, the Sumaah included, take their instruction from Bastion.
t.Feroz: The Senate's invitation to the Suranni ended with the rebel camp's occupants enslaved, which deeply shocked the Freeborn. Only Severin's sermon has kept people from speaking out and appealing to the Synod.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is home to the sermon's author, Severin von Holberg, and to the radical Bishop Orlando di Holberg of the University of Holberg.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: the territory's only link is the constitutional scholar Teodora Bezavina of Delev, who speaks for the moderates seeking to curb the National Assemblies.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Mournwold slaughter is cited as still fresh in the minds of many in the West.
t.Spiral: The Iron Helms struck the heart of the Black Plateau, killing hundreds of Imperial soldiers through magical whiplash and madness. Severin's sermon has stifled calls for the Synod to act over it.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: Mentioned in passing: Holmauer is named as one of the places where congregations heard Severin's sermon.

Change.d: Until the Summer Solstice, every Imperial mine and forest produced six ingots or measures of random materials in place of part of its usual yield. Scholars judged the effect to be neither curse nor enchantment. Casting Wondrous Forests of the Night or Bright Eyes Gleam in the Depths across the Empire could intensify it, and the Eight-spoked Wheel and Retrograde Wheel were more potent at the Equinox. The heralds Centimani and Alkahest vanished, and the old eternals could no longer be contacted. Their sealed regio reopened with altered magic. Azoth's herald promised that its spirits would come to Anvil at the Summer Solstice. Distil the Serpent's Stone was permanently changed so that it produced shadow eggs.

n.Dawn: A glade of night-blooming flowers in Semmerholm, once tied to the old eternals, now gives anyone who sleeps there vivid dreams of living wildly different lives. Dawn's mines and forests are also affected by the strange yields.
n.Imperial Orcs: Orc miners share in the upheaval: a liberated orc in Skarsind struck what looked like copper and found ambergelt gushing out instead.
n.Navarr: Navarri lands were changed twice over: dragonbone clay in Miaren crystallised into tempest jade, and the Senate's alchemical tower at Holtford vanished, leaving a strange pool in its place.
n.The Marches: Marcher mines such as the Green Iron mines beneath Whittle Hill produced swarms of insects and cocoons, and the earlier harvesting of corpses in the Mournwold is named among the signs of the old eternals' work.
n.Wintermark: A beggarwood grove in Kallavesa, where mystics once met heralds of Murit, now comes alive at night with drifting lights whispering in unknown tongues.

t.Kallavesa: The Kallavesa beggarwood grove once used for meetings with Murit's heralds now fills at night with iridescent lights that whisper in a dozen unknown tongues.
t.Miaren: Soft dragonbone clay beneath Miaren's trees crystallised into crimson tempest jade, and the Holtford alchemical workshop was transformed.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the harvesting of corpses in the Mournwold is cited as one of the signs of Murit and Soghter's activity over the previous months.
t.Semmerholm: A night-blooming glade in Semmerholm, its regio reopened, now gives sleepers incredibly vivid dreams of living wildly different lives.
t.Skarsind: A liberated orc mining in Skarsind struck what seemed a copper vein, only for thick ambergelt to gush out, one example of the transformed mine yields.

r.Miaren/Holtford: The Senate-built white granite tower dedicated to Murit collapsed and vanished, leaving a painfully cold pool. It shows visitors who they might have been and reflects stars unlike the real sky, and locals say a creature rises from it at half moon to speak with Night scholars.

City lights.d: Gains from the newly finished Blood Red Roads lifted almost every citizen's income, but League bravos and mountebanks lost their income to bite, whose price and violence were rising; the Senate could outlaw it and fund magistrates with 25 thrones a season. In Siroc, Safya i Kalamar i Guerra of the Glass Parador refused the Full Sails Carta's offer to buy out fleeing Freeborn, boosting Madrugan production. Siroc merchants offered to help fund a new shipyard until the Summer Solstice. Ambassador Mila Eisenfalke believed the Commonwealth would garrison a Siroc fortification, and Menno Van Ritsjhof might design coastal defences. Suaq and Steinr merchants proposed the Kalpaheim Runehall, needing 60 wains of white granite.

n.Grendel: The Grendel, holding Atalaya and all of Free Landing and raiding Lightsea, are the threat Siroc is defying, and the proposed shipyard and sea defences are aimed squarely at resisting them.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as one of the westward routes from Kalpaheim made easier by the Blood Red Roads.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia is named as a neighbour that trades with Hahnmark and lies on a road from Kalpaheim.
n.The Brass Coast: Madrugan businesses gain an extra rank of production thanks to the Mistress of the Glass Parador's call to stand firm, and Siroc's merchants offer to help fund a new shipyard to replace the one burned at Atalaya.
n.The League: League bravos and mountebanks lose their income to bite as drug violence spreads through the cities, the Full Sails Carta's opportunistic offer in Siroc was rebuffed, and the League National Assembly could urge Menno Van Ritsjhof to design Siroc's sea defences.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: Little Whittle carries Mournwold green iron to Tassato, and Upwold and Marcher neighbours are named as Hahnmark's established trade routes.
n.Wintermark: Suaq and Steinr merchants, aided by the runesmith-engineers Hurik and Manun, propose a Kalpaheim Runehall to exploit the Blood Red Roads, offering either extra coin or mine resources to Hahnmark businesses if commissioned and built.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the page notes the Commonwealth could not feasibly move an army to the Bay of Catazar.
t.Hahnmark: Merchants propose the Kalpaheim Runehall, which would take six months and 60 wains of white granite and grant Hahnmark businesses either 1060 coins a season (Bargains) or a share of 60 mine resources (Wealth); the opportunity lasts until the end of the Autumn Equinox.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia is named as a trading neighbour of Hahnmark and a route west from Kalpaheim.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is named as a destination Wintermark merchants can now reach quickly on the Blood Red Roads.
t.Madruga: Every business in Madruga gains an extra rank of production this season, and Siroc is offered a cheaper new shipyard until the end of the Summer Solstice plus possible Commonwealth-garrisoned or Van Ritsjhof-designed defences against the Grendel.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: Little Whittle is noted as bringing green iron from the Mournwold to Tassato.
t.Sarvos: Bite has become so sought after that a dose fetches three or four crowns in parts of Sarvos, amid violence against dealers; the city's Colossus and markets are also noted as drawing foreign visitors.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Segura is not named; it shares only in the general Empire-wide trade boost described.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the northern borders of Sermersuaq are used to compare travel times from Kalpaheim.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as a westward route from Kalpaheim eased by the Blood Red Roads.
t.Tassato: A rumour about stolen bite sparked armed clashes across the river between Regario and Mestra that left two dead and dozens seriously injured, and resentments continue to simmer.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold is named as the road south from Kalpaheim that was once hard going for wagons.

r.Madruga/Free Landing: Free Landing, including Atalaya where the Grendel burned the shipyard, is described as wholly in Grendel hands.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: Mentioned in passing: Grendel raiders are described looting north and south along the Lightsea coast, with Quzar already looted.
r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: Mestran bravos, enraged by a rumour that Regarians had intercepted their bite shipment, crossed the river by boat and fought deadly clashes, and many Mestrans still blame the thieving Regarians.
r.Tassato/Tassato Regario: Regario mountebanks were rumoured to have intercepted a bite shipment, drawing armed Mestran bravos across the river; Regarians dismiss the anger as proof the Mestrans are drug-addled.

Come back to stay.d: Research circulated at Lord Armand Remys's request claimed that Varkula's tomb has three doors, two reportedly opened when Holberg and Skarsind fell, and that the third might now open. People sleeping in Casinea dreamt of a wolf-toothed woman in a crown of black ice berating the Empire for losing Zenith. The Senate interior gained an aura of suspicion and paranoia, blamed by some on Varkula's ghost. An i Tamazir i Riqueza scribe of the House of Quills, whose family executed her will, was seen travelling cagily to Anvil. In Necropolis an unfamiliar bell tolled at midnight, a former tomb guard began preaching that the tomb had been torn open, and the tomb was found barred from outside with the ground before it consecrated to Vigilance.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: a Necropolis citizen grumbles that the Imperatrix should bring Dawn and Navarr to heel.
n.Druj: The Druj conquest of Zenith is the loss that supposedly stirred Varkula's spirit, and the dreams demand that the Druj-held territory be reclaimed immediately.
n.Highguard: The Highborn face unrest at home: Varkula's tomb in Necropolis was found barred and consecrated to Vigilance, and a former tomb guard preaches that her spirit was woken by the defeat of the joined Highborn armies at Zenith.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: some Varushkans darkly suggest Varkula might not regard Skarsind, now held by the Imperial Orcs, as truly in Imperial hands.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the House of Quills scribe was spotted at the Navarr wayhouse of Myfanwy's Rest, and a citizen grumbles that Navarr should be brought to heel.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn House of Quills, the i Tamazir i Riqueza family who executed Varkula's will, are drawn into the rumours after one of them was seen travelling secretively to Anvil.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the earlier fall of Holberg is recalled as the time one of the tomb's doors supposedly opened.
n.Urizen: Many in Urizen see the dreams as proof that losing their territory of Zenith has called Varkula back, and that it must be retaken at once to avert her vengeance.
n.Varushka: Varushkans reportedly experience the Casinea dreams more often, and some suggest the Winterborn might not consider Skarsind truly Imperial.

t.Casinea: People sleeping in Casinea suffered dreams of a crowned, wolf-toothed woman condemning the loss of Zenith, waking confused and weakened.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: stories recall loud noises from the tomb when Holberg fell to the orcs, though it has since been liberated.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: most relatives of the i Tamazir i Riqueza family of the House of Quills still live in Madruga.
t.Necropolis: In the Black City an unfamiliar bell tolled at midnight, preachers proclaimed Varkula's return, and her tomb was found barred from outside with the ground before it consecrated to Vigilance.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind's fall supposedly opened a door of the tomb, and no closing was heard when it returned to the Empire.
t.Zenith: Zenith's fall to the Druj, as the first territory Varkula added to the Empire, is the trigger for all the omens of her return.

r.Necropolis/Fishguard: Mentioned in passing: Fishguard is not named; it is attached as part of Necropolis, where Varkula's tomb and the preaching are found.

Coming home.d: The civil service could find no military purpose for the conjunction, which opened near the bridge of Guthwulf of the Red Embrace. Kallavesi mystics said it was meant for a pilgrimage to the marsh's dead, last seen in Emperor Guntherm's reign. Only one nation could pass through. The Masi prepared to receive the host, and stormcrows were asked to choose three recent fallen heroes and three speakers. Consecrating the marsh grove to Pride with true liao would raise Wintermark's ability to support armies to four, honouring Inga Tarn and Isenbrad. Gunnbrand's mandate was enacted, so Wintermark armies fighting the Jotun gain victory but inflict fewer casualties, and the Fist of the Mountains and Green Shield may each update their army's quality once.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Emperor Guntherm's body lies in state in Bastion rather than in the marsh, which some Wintermark folk quietly resent.
n.Jotun: Wintermark's enacted mandate means its armies will now fight the Jotun as honourable equals, gaining more victory but inflicting a fifth fewer casualties. The change will be visible to everyone in any territory where such a campaign is fought.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Mourne is cited as the point when relations between Wintermark and the Jotun took a darker turn.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: in Guntherm's reign, Wintermark and Jotun warriors briefly joined forces to fight the Thule.
n.Wintermark: The whole nation was offered a pilgrimage to inter and honour its dead in the Kallavesa Marsh, with the chance to win permanent extra army capacity by consecrating the grove to Pride with true liao. Its Assembly's heroism mandate was enacted, permanently changing how its armies fight the Jotun and giving two of its generals a chance to update their armies.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: Emperor Guntherm's body lies in state here, not in the Kallavesa swamp.
t.Kallavesa: The conjunction opened into the heart of Kallavesa's great swamp, where the Masi readied a traditional welcome and song for the Wintermark pilgrims and any fallen heroes brought to be interred.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Mourne is named as the turning point after which Wintermark's battles with the Jotun grew more threatening.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun armies in Stark are noted to be far from the conjunction's destination, ruling out a military purpose.

r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: The marsh, resting place of Empress Britta, Inga Tarn and Isenbrad, was the pilgrimage destination. A Pride consecration of its central grove with true liao would be guarded by the Masi and lost only if an enemy conquered and despoiled the region.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun armies in Stark are too far away to explain the conjunction.

Construct Blade of Thorn.d: Proposed by the senator for Hercynia and seconded by Miaren, the motion commissioned a great work in Old Ranging to produce mana. Its spiral is to include stones honouring those who gave their lives in defence of others, and it was framed as a gesture of goodwill from Achilles of Damokan's Forge to the Navarr and a reminder that the Empire stands united even in its darkest days. It cost 40 wains of mithril and 10 thrones in labour. Both sums were received from Rhisiart Dancewalker after the Spring Equinox 382YE. The great work does not create an Imperial title.

n.Navarr: The Navarr received a mana-producing great work in their territory of Hercynia, offered as a gesture of goodwill from Achilles of Damokan's Forge and paid for by Rhisiart Dancewalker.

t.Hercynia: Hercynia's senator proposed the commission, and the territory gained Llafndrián, a great work that supplies mana to the owners of mana sites.

r.Hercynia/Old Ranging: Old Ranging is the site of the Blade of Thorn, whose spiral bears memorial stones to those who died defending others.

Construct Brenna’s Gift.d: Raised in Spring 382YE through Jorgen Brenna's Imperial Wayleave, the motion proposed a great work in Hahnmark to boost farming income, and it passed. Beyond standard costs, it required 40 wains of weirwood and 80 crowns in labour. Jorgen Brenna supplied both the weirwood and the crowns after the Spring Equinox 382YE. Once completed, the work will provide money split between the owners of farms in Hahnmark. The page notes that the region of Hahnmark in which the great work will stand has still to be settled.

n.Wintermark: A Wintermark-held territory gains a work meant to enrich its farmers, funded entirely by Jorgen Brenna's own weirwood and coin.

t.Hahnmark: Brenna's Gift is to be built in Hahnmark, and once complete it will share extra money among the territory's farm owners, though its exact region is still to be decided.

Construct Golden Causeway.d: Proposed by Astolat and seconded by Weirwater, the motion seized an opportunity offered to the Empire by the Lady of the Semmerlak, and it passed at 220 thrones. It used non-standard costs of 25 wains of white granite, 15 wains of mithril and 10 thrones in labour, with no upkeep. Bohemond De Rondell provided all of these materials and funds after the Spring Equinox 382YE. Once complete, the causeway will let the armies of Dawn, and only Dawn, march from Lacuve to the region on the far side of the Semmerlak and return the same way. If the Conclave were to place the eternal the Lady of the Lake serves, currently Eleonaris, under enmity, the causeway could not be used until the enmity was lifted.

n.Dawn: Proposed by Astolat and seconded by Weirwater, the causeway will give Dawn's armies alone a route from Lacuve across the Semmerlak and back, and Bohemond De Rondell supplied the granite, mithril and thrones needed to build it.
n.Druj: The causeway opens a passage across the Semmerlak into Druj-held lands, through which Dawnish armies will be able to march once it is complete.

t.The Semmerlak: The Golden Causeway will be raised across the uncontrolled Semmerlak at the Lady of the Semmerlak's offer, linking Lacuve to the region on the opposite shore for Dawnish armies.

Construct Iron Qanat.d: Proposed by Tassato and seconded by Kahraman, the motion sought to take advantage of an opportunity presented by settlers from the Isle of Zemress. It was to be overseen by Almodin Oktístis, Priest of the Builder, at a cost of 50 wains of weirwood, 50 wains of white granite and 200 crowns, taking a year to build with upkeep of 10 thrones a season. Once complete, the Iron Qanat and its Water Tower would have let the Brass Coast support an additional army or navy and upgraded Red Plains Farm and the Golden Terraces. However, after the Senate fired the Asavean Architect, construction could not be completed, and the motion lapsed at the start of the Spring Equinox 383YE.

n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast stood to gain the capacity to support an additional army or navy from the Iron Qanat, but lost that prospect when the Asavean Architect was fired and the commission lapsed unbuilt.

t.Segura: Segura was to host the fortified Iron Qanat and its protective Water Tower, which would have upgraded Red Plains Farm and the Golden Terraces, but construction was never completed there.

Construct Kruidenkenner warehouse.d: Proposed by the Necropolis senator and seconded by Casinea's, the motion passed at 40 Thrones. It used non-standard costs of 8 wains of weirwood and 16 crowns of labour, and Thanmir Hrafnar supplied both after the Spring Equinox. When complete, the ministry creates the Imperial title of Kruidenkenner Trademaster, appointed by public auction through the Imperial Bourse. The senator asked that it be called "The Kruidenkenner magazijn" and that the appointment take place in Spring. The Civil Service agreed a Spring appointment was appropriate but noted the motion could not stipulate it. If Spring is set, the first auction will follow completion for a short term.

n.Highguard: Highguard's senator for Necropolis proposed the motion, which brings a new trade ministry and its Imperial title onto Highborn-held land at Crown's Quay.

t.Necropolis: Crown's Quay in Necropolis is the chosen site for the Kruidenkenner warehouse, which will give the Empire access to Cerulean Mazzarine from Sarcophan Delves herbalists.

Construct Lorenzo's Great Game.d: Proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Reikos, the motion commissioned a great work of white granite in Temeschwar, a gaming house and casino to be known as "Lorenzo's Great Game", funded by the Guild of Good Game. It cost 40 wains of white granite and 10 thrones in labour, with three months to construct. After the Spring Equinox the materials and money were received from Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar. The commission is overseen by Almodin Oktístis, Priest of the Builder, and as a great work it provides additional income to business owners in Temeschwar.

n.The League: A League citizen, Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar, paid for a great work that brings additional income to business owners in one of the League's cities.

t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar gains Lorenzo's Great Game, a white granite gaming house and casino that provides additional income to business owners in the territory.

Construct Peak Edge trading enclave.d: Proposed under an Imperial Wayleave by Selenius, the commission was counted as a single commission and was self-funded. It carried non-standard costs: 12 wains of weirwood, 12 wains of white granite and 48 crowns in labour. After the Spring Equinox 382YE, Selenius supplied the weirwood, the granite and 24 crowns. The commission was completed, creating a trading post that allows trade with the Khiklotu Khrysoú of Axos for both mana and valuable materials. It also created a new Imperial title, the Eastern Broker, to be appointed by unanimous agreement of the Navarr senators.

n.Navarr: The Navarr senators gained the right to appoint the new Eastern Broker, but only by unanimous agreement, giving the nation control over the Empire's new trading link with the Axou.

t.Therunin: The Peak Edge trading enclave was built in Therunin, making the Navarr-held territory home to a trading post for mana and valuable materials from the Khiklotu Khrysoú of Axos.

Construct Virtue's Rest.d: Proposed by Bastion and seconded by Bregasland, the motion created a network of hostels offering safety and rest to pilgrims travelling to and from the White City. The work cost 100 wains of white granite and 200 crowns in labour, and took six months. Rhesa of the Scions of Ravenfell provided both halves of the materials and coin, after the Winter Solstice 382YE and the Summer Solstice 383YE. Once finished, it yields 50 liao and 100 Synod votes spread among Bastion's congregations. The hostels were designed to line the proposed Blood Red Roads and gave only half benefit until the White Roads were completed shortly before the Winter Solstice 384YE. Philemon refused to let any League "montebanc" near the scheme.

n.Highguard: The motion called for Highguard's citizens to fund the work themselves, and Rhesa of the Highborn Scions of Ravenfell supplied all the granite and coin, giving the nation a pilgrim network and extra liao and Synod votes for its Bastion congregations.

t.Bastion: Seven Virtue hostels were built across Bastion to shelter pilgrims to the White City. They provide 50 liao and 100 Synod votes to its congregations, at full strength only once the White Roads reached the territory before Winter 384YE.

Construct sausage shop.d: Proposed by the senator for Holberg and seconded by Temeschwar, the motion arose from an opportunity to expand sausage production and distribution in Holberg. It used non-standard costs of 20 wains of white granite and 40 crowns of labour, with no annual upkeep. The materials were to be provided by Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar of the Bloody Butcher's Guild, who delivered 20 wains of white granite and 5 thrones after the Spring Equinox. Once complete, the work would give a bounty of two thrones and four rings shared among every farm owner in Holberg. It would also spread the distinctive Holberg travelling ration wherever good sausages are sold.

n.The League: The League's senators gain the new Imperial title of Custodian of the Bloody Great Sausage to appoint each year by unanimous decision, and a League guildsman from Temeschwar funded the work.

t.Holberg: The Great Work is to be built in Holberg to honour the provisioners of its siege. When complete, it will share a bounty among every farm owner there and spread the Holberg travelling ration across the Empire.

Construct seminary in Reikos.d: Proposed by Casinea and seconded by Tassato, the motion called for a Great Work: an artificial lake replacing the drained pools at the Vigilant Swan so the swans might return, a deliberate statement to the Druj that whatever they destroy can be rebuilt better. At its centre would stand a seminary training magisters of Highguard in magic and Virtue. Standard costs applied, and Nira of Cantiarch's Hold supplied 40 wains of white granite and 10 thrones after the Spring Equinox. The seminary was completed and benefits mana site owners in Reikos, though it creates no Imperial title. The exact nature of the benefit was left undefined, pending detail from the senator.

n.Druj: The rebuilt lake and seminary were framed as a direct answer to the Druj, proof that what they destroyed at the Vigilant Swan could be restored and improved.
n.Highguard: Highguard gained a completed seminary to train its magisters in magic and Virtue, funded in part by Nira of Cantiarch's Hold's donation of white granite and thrones.

t.Reikos: The drained pools at the Vigilant Swan were replaced by an artificial lake with a seminary at its heart, which now benefits the territory's mana site owners, though the precise benefit remained unspecified.

Construct summer sinecure.d: Using the power to commission mana structures, the Arcane Architect declared the construction of a highly efficient, self-funded summer sinecure in Reikos. Its cost was unknown, and after the Summer Solstice 382YE Vittore provided 3 white granite, 3 weirwood and 12 crowns towards it. The Architect still needed to supply further details, including the region and how the title would be appointed. Because the Architect's powers strictly covered structures producing crystal mana, and summer vis is not crystal mana, the Constitutional Court asked the Senate for guidance; Senators confirmed they intended vis-producing structures to fall within the Architect's remit. The Architect was assumed to hold a suitable opportunity.

n.Highguard: As holder of Reikos, Highguard would see a new summer vis sinecure and its Imperial title, Keeper of the Cox, established within its lands once the work is completed.

t.Reikos: Reikos was named as the site of the planned summer sinecure, though the specific region within the territory had still to be specified by the Arcane Architect.

Construct the Azure Chorus.d: Raised under an Imperial Wayleave by Lorenzo la Volpe, the motion called for a congregational sinecure for the Brass Coast in Braydon's Jasse, Kahraman. Its holder would be chosen by the Freeborn assembly and serve for life or until resignation. The cost was 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns, which Lorenzo agreed to pay, and the motion stipulated that the title must not include the words Bloody, Red, Cleavers or Butchers. The motion passed, and Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar supplied the materials and money after the Spring Equinox. When completed, it will create an Imperial title, the Azure Sutannir, appointed by the Freeborn national assembly.

n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn will gain a new congregational sinecure, whose holder, the Azure Sutannir, is to be appointed by the Freeborn national assembly.

t.Kahraman: Kahraman, held by the Brass Coast, is where the Azure Chorus is to be built. Its materials and labour were paid for after the Spring Equinox.

r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: Braydon's Jasse is the chosen site for the Azure Chorus, which is to be built there with 10 wains of white granite.

Construct venom brokerage.d: Proposed by the senator for Miaren and seconded by Therunin, the motion answered an opportunity offered by the brokers of Navarr to build a brokerage dedicated to tools for fighting the vallorn. It passed, with non-standard costs of 30 weirwood and 60 crowns in labour. After the Spring Equinox, Llewelyn Leafstalker supplied 30 wains of weirwood and 7 Thrones 4 Crowns. Once complete, the brokerage, named Honest Twill's Gardening Supplies, will create a new Imperial title, the Blackroot Broker, appointed by unanimous decision of the senators of Navarr.

n.Navarr: Navarr's senators will appoint the Blackroot Broker by unanimous decision, giving the nation control of a new supply of herbs, blade venoms and Scorpion Stings for its war against the vallorn, with the materials provided by Llewelyn Leafstalker.

t.Miaren: Miaren is to host the brokerage Honest Twill's Gardening Supplies, which will become a source of herbs, venoms and Scorpion Stings once construction is complete.

Disburse funds for Farstrider's Watch Sp.d: The Senator for Mournwold proposed the motion and Upwold seconded it. It released Senate funds set aside for building the fort named Farstrider's Watch in the Greensward region of the Mournwold. It passed at 80 Thrones, and the money was disbursed to the Senator for Mournwold to buy the materials needed for construction. The page records the release of the funds only. It does not say whether the fortification was finished.

n.The Marches: Marcher senators drove the motion, with Mournwold proposing and Upwold seconding. Its passage put Senate money in Marcher hands to fortify a territory they had reclaimed.

t.Mournwold: The Senator for Mournwold received the disbursed funds to buy materials for a new fortification within the territory.

r.Mournwold/Greensward: The Greensward is the planned site of Farstrider's Watch, and the materials paid for by this motion are meant for its construction there.

Dispatch prospectors to the Pride of Ikk.d: Proposed by the senator for Hahnmark and seconded by Kallavesa, the motion described itself as self-funded, but the costs actually fell to the Senate: 10 Thrones. Hengest Dun donated 10 Thrones to the treasury to cover it. The prospectors returned shortly after the Summer Solstice 382YE and confirmed that the workings could be expanded significantly, though not cheaply. The Senate could commission the expansion for 400 Thrones; the work would take six months, after which the mine's output would rise from 15 to 20 wains of mithril each season.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark's senators for Hahnmark and Kallavesa proposed and seconded the motion, which established that a Winterfolk mithril mine could be enlarged if the Senate funded a 400-Throne expansion.

t.Sermersuaq: Prospectors surveyed the Pride of Ikka's Tears in Sermersuaq and found that its mithril output could be raised from 15 to 20 wains a season through a six-month, 400-Throne expansion.

Everything has rhythm.d: In Spiral, Iron Helms soldiers driven mad by the Black Plateau roamed Ossuary, and the Grendel arranged to hand over Dogri Thulebane's body at Blue Haven. Jotun Raðljóst who had found the Pride of Ikka's Tears mithril mine had to be stopped in Suaq Wastes. Grendel moridun fortified Free Landing. Feni raiders spread from Upwold into the Mournwold. Husks and merrow mages crossed the East Floes. Surut asked the Navarr to bring Winter's Flame to two vallorn regio in West Ranging. A warlock-led warband, possibly Thule, raided Volodmartz mines. A rescue of at least two hundred Highborn prisoners was possible at Ceramic Meander in Zenith. Each was an opportunity, not a settled outcome.

n.Druj: Chikad warriors guarded the Ceramic Meander camp holding Highborn prisoners, where a Tepel apothecary poisoned one captive each day, while Druj warbands took selected prisoners towards the Barrens.
n.Grendel: Speaker Morna arranged to return Dogri Thulebane's remains at Blue Haven. In Madruga, elite moridun organised leftover raiders and pirates behind new defences, and Imperial conjunctions were set to strike them.
n.Highguard: Highborn soldiers captured during the retreat from Zenith faced brutal treatment, and a rescue could return at least two hundred to the Granite Pillar, Valiant Pegasus and Seventh Wave. The Citadel Guard's camp in Spiral was also threatened by frenzied soldiers.
n.Jotun: Raðljóst pathfinders who had discovered the Imperial mithril mine were heading back to their Jarls in two bands. Prognosticators warned the find might redirect the Jotun invasion north towards Suaq Wastes and Suaq Fount.
n.Navarr: Surut's heralds asked the Navarr to keep leading his fires against the vallorn, wanting Brennos Brackensong, general of the Quiet Step, to be the focus of Winter's Flame at both West Ranging regio.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn corsairs had helped liberate Lightsea and Free Landing in Madruga. Conjunctions offered a chance to break the Grendel redoubts so Imperial forces could swiftly retake the Free Landing islands.
