n.The Marches: Marcher lands faced spreading Feni raids through Upwold and into the Mournwold, and the Towerjacks' camp in Spiral was threatened by frenzied soldiers. Marchers had also fought in Madruga and were asked to join the Navarr against the vallorn.
n.Thule: An orc and husk warband led by a warlock raiding Volodmartz mines strongly appeared to be Thule, though it was unconfirmed and was unusually not taking slaves.
n.Urizen: The Winter Sun's camp in Ossuary was among those threatened by the frenzied Iron Helms. Urizen egregores identified the conjunction to Blue Haven for Dogri Thulebane's handover.
n.Varushka: About a hundred Iron Helms soldiers succumbed to the Black Plateau's Night Magic and became murderous bands, and Varushkans might wish to deal with them. Volodmartz also suffered raids on its mines.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark was offered the return of Dogri Thulebane's body and the chance to protect the mithril mine held by seat holder Algar of Ashenhall. It also faced husks rising on the East Floes, while the Feni threat in Hahnmark seemed to have eased.

t.Hahnmark: The Feni raids that troubled Wood Heath spread into Southridge but have since largely abated, for reasons still unclear.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: named as the territory next to Sealtoq, which a Jotun shift north might spare.
t.Liathaven: Two conjunctions to the remaining Spring regio in West Ranging offered the chance to burn them with Surut's flame, weaken the vallorn and secure a beachhead in the territory.
t.Madruga: After Lightsea and Free Landing were liberated, Grendel moridun dug in remaining raiders behind defences, and three conjunctions offered a chance to clear them.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: Blue Haven, the handover point for Dogri Thulebane's body, lies near the border with Mareave.
t.Mournwold: Feni raids crossed into the Mournwold, sacking thrall farms. If they were not stopped at Connor's Rock, every farm and business there would lose 36 rings and every herb garden two herbs.
t.Sermersuaq: Jotun pathfinders who found the mithril mine could be intercepted in Suaq Wastes, while husks accompanied by living merrow mages marched inland across the East Floes.
t.Spiral: The Black Plateau awoke in Screed, driving Imperial soldiers mad and turning some Iron Helms into killers in Ossuary. Apulus hosted the handover of Dogri Thulebane's remains.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Druj slave parties were thought to be taking a circuitous route around Therunin to the Barrens.
t.Upwold: The Feni warband in Birchland swelled to two or three units and raided homesteads, monasteries and market towns across Ashbrook and Tower March.
t.Volodmartz: A warlock-led warband of orcs and husks, possibly Thule, raided mine caravans for gold, gems and orichalcum, and a conjunction offered a chance to confront it near Veltsgorsk.
t.Zenith: Highborn prisoners were held at a Druj camp in Iteri, and two conjunctions offered a chance to rescue them across the Utique.

r.Hahnmark/Southridge: Feni attacks crossed into the hills of Southridge about a month after the Winter Solstice but have since abated significantly.
r.Hahnmark/Wood Heath: The Winter Solstice attempt to strike the Feni warband here failed, and its raids continued before spreading into Southridge.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: Conjunctions to Silent Stand and Far Steading offered battle against vallorn husks and creatures amid a venomous miasma. Success at both would give the Empire control of the whole region.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: Mentioned in passing: success in West Ranging would let Imperial forces push into Westwood without fear for their supply lines.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Grendel moridun built redoubts and stockades on the islands, and conjunctions to Summer's Stone at Halcorim, Estavia's Key and the Isle of Seven Goats offered a chance to drive them back.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: Mentioned in passing: its liberation from the Grendel was described as swift and decisive.
r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: A conjunction to Connor's Rock offered a chance to stop the Feni as their raids pushed westwards into the Chalkdowns.
r.Mournwold/Freemoor: Several thrall farms in Freemoor were thoroughly sacked by Feni raiders.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: Husks rose from the lakes, accompanied by living merrow mages, and two large conjunctions to Iqaluit Rise and Pangnirtung Station offered battle against them.
r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: Prognosticators suggested the mithril find might draw the Jotun invasion away from populous Sealtoq.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun armies had crossed into Stark, and one band of pathfinders was returning to them there.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: Prognosticators suggested the Jotun might divert their invasion north to claim Suaq Fount because of the mithril.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: Jotun pathfinders could be intercepted at West Bay and Bitter Tundra, and none were to be left alive so the Jarls would not learn of the mithril mine. The Jotun might yet turn north to claim the region.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: Mentioned in passing: Jotun armies were in Tanikipari, and one band of pathfinders was returning towards them.
r.Spiral/Apulus: The Grendel funeral escort waited at Blue Haven, a cove in south-eastern Apulus, to hand over Dogri Thulebane's remains to a small Imperial party.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: Frenzied Iron Helms soldiers roamed Ossuary threatening Imperial camps, and conjunctions to the Nephan Traps offered a chance to intercept them by calming, subduing or killing them.
r.Spiral/Screed: The Black Plateau had awoken, and Night Magic pouring out of Screed drove soldiers to madness.
r.Upwold/Ashbrook: Homesteads, monasteries and market towns in Ashbrook were targeted by the growing Feni warband.
r.Upwold/Birchland: The Feni warband here survived a failed Solstice strike and swelled to the equivalent of two or three military units.
r.Upwold/Tower March: Homesteads, monasteries and market towns in Tower March were targeted by the spreading Feni raids.
r.Volodmartz/Brez: The raiding warband was last seen heading towards the White Granite mine at Veltsgorsk in Brez.
r.Volodmartz/Opascari: A conjunction for fifteen people opened to the road near the Granites of Veltsgorsk, listed under Opascari, to confront the warlock's warband.
r.Zenith/Iteri: Conjunctions to the Ceramic Meander Slave Camp and Ceramic Meadows offered a chance to distract and hold off the Chikad while Highborn prisoners escaped.

Fight.d: The Marcher and Imperial Orc assemblies each sent a priest with 50 doses of liao. Working together, the two recruited dozens of preachers. They found the thralls peaceful, unarmed, and very like their Marcher neighbours, and already well informed about the virtues. The news that the Senate had recognised them as foreigners, so they would not be driven from their land, was met with relief. Yet as the priests explained the doctrines of the Way, crowds became upset or hostile and drove them off. The thralls' influential figures, the timber merchant Sigdór and Hamma the Lame of Eversweet Orchard, asked to meet the priests at Anvil. Persuading them would bring many thralls to the faith.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc Assembly sent Bloodcrow Losak to preach to the thralls. Hamma had also been invited to meet Bloodcrow Yargol, the Advisor for Orc Affairs, and Bloodcrow Morghur, the orc General of the Winter Sun.
n.Jotun: The Jotun thralls of the Mournwold were relieved to keep their land, but their response to the Way turned from interest to angry rejection. They say their leaders are the Jotun jarls, though in daily matters figures like Sigdór and Hamma hold real sway.
n.The Marches: The Marcher Assembly sent Sister Meredith with liao to convert the thralls. Many Marchers of the Mourn already treated the thralls as neighbours or friends, trading with them and playing foot the ball together.

t.Mournwold: The Marcher-held Mournwold was home to a large population of Jotun thralls on prized farmland. Efforts to bring them to the Way stalled there, pending talks with their leaders at Anvil.

r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: The Chalkdowns was one of the key regions occupied by Jotun thralls, where preachers met interest that soured into hostility.
r.Mournwold/Green March: Green March was one of the key regions held by the Jotun thralls targeted by the preaching mission.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Mentioned in passing: the thrall leader Sigdór, a timber merchant, lived on the edge of the Greensward.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Southmoor was one of the key regions occupied by Jotun thralls, where the priests' sermons were received first with interest and then with anger.

Free to live.d: Backed unanimously by the Freeborn Assembly, the Islanders settled the Sobral Grasses and Yellow Chase with almost all their possessions, even livestock. They proposed the Iron Qanat irrigation works, or a fortified Water Tower variant, for the Grasses, and the Black Locks canals on the Scorrero. They also asked the Conclave and Spring Archmage to seek a Spring eternal to transform the arid Yellow Chase. Their tribal heritage is unknown and some may not descend from a Founder, so the egregore is reluctant to swear more of them. Horror at the Iron Confederacy slaughtering rebels in Feroz has halted oath-taking entirely, and some Islanders question whether another nation might suit them better.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: as the would-be conquerors and enslavers of the Isle of Zemress, whose navy the Empire evaded and whom the Islanders still fear.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Islanders are described as almost as devout as any Highborn citizen, and the transformation of Highborn-held Reikos inspired their Yellow Chase plan.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn gained a hard-working new population with offers of great works that could feed an extra army or navy and enrich local fleets and congregations. However, unresolved questions of tribe and doctrine have stopped Islanders swearing to the egregore, and some now doubt they chose the right nation.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Scorrero is described as the fastest and most turbulent of the great rivers that pour into the Bay.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: news that the Iron Confederacy was invited to slaughter the rebels sheltering in Feroz horrified the abolitionist Islanders and halted their integration.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the eternal Llofir's transformation of Reikos inspired the Islanders' hope that a Spring eternal might revive the Yellow Chase, though they noted it came at some cost.
t.Segura: Segura, still recovering from the Lasambrian orc conquest, was being revitalised by the Islanders' new farms. The proposed Black Locks would open the Scorrero to trade and pay rings to every fleet and congregation in the territory, and a Water Tower would fortify the whole territory.

r.Segura/Sobral Grasses: Hundreds of Islander farms have turned the once barren Grasses into busy grain land, though water and soil are poor. The proposed Iron Qanat or Water Tower would irrigate every farm and upgrade the Red Plains Farm and Golden Terraces.
r.Segura/Yellow Chase: The Chase proved too arid and rocky for crops, supporting little more than sheep and goats. The Islanders asked the Conclave and the Spring Archmage to consider persuading a Spring eternal to transform it.

Heroes.d: After the Autumn Equinox 381YE, Suranni rebels set up camps in Feroz and raided Kalino. The Senate backed Ambassador Zadkiel de Coeurdefer in inviting the Duke of Kalino to intervene. The Freeborn assembly denounced the rebels as heretics, and the Assembly of the Nine urged that refugees who could be brought to the Way be offered succour. A fortnight after the Winter Solstice, five thousand Suranni soldiers destroyed the camps. Fighters were killed and hung from trees, survivors were chained and returned to slavery, and the ringleader Ahraz Reborn was torn apart by templars. A few escaped, some perhaps given sanctuary. The army remains camped in Fontargenta, and the Duke is sending a delegation to Anvil to thank the Ambassador.

n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn assembly denounced the rebels as heretics and blasphemers, and Freeborn citizens refused them succour, handing some over to the Suranni. Yet the tale of a drover secretly adopting two rebel children shows not everyone turned them away.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the bay is not named, but the opening tale takes place on a clifftop coast road where a drover throws a rebel boy's amulet over the cliff into the sea.
t.Feroz: Five thousand of the Duke of Kalino's soldiers crossed into Feroz, destroyed the rebel camps, hung fighters from trees along the border and hunted down fleeing rebels across the territory.
t.Kalino: The rebellion against the Duke of Kalino was crushed, and captured rebels were marched back in chains to slavery in his mines and fields. The delighted Duke is sending a delegation to Anvil to thank the Imperial Ambassador.

r.Feroz/Fontargenta: The Duke of Kalino's army is camped in Fontargenta awaiting new orders, and is expected to return to Kalino once the last revolutionaries are captured.

How sweet is the sea.d: Captains from every Imperial nation took part in mapping the Bay, with civil service coordination and Senate funds. Just over half were Freeborn, and Dawn sent a sizable contingent. Each fleet received half its usual privateering income, paid partly by patrons and partly by raids on Grendel vessels, along with a copy of the map and a gazetteer. The map is not detailed enough for magicians, but it fills gaps in Imperial geography. It was made public after the Spring Equinox. Grendel pirates, some devoted to the eternal Siakha and aided by sharks, heralds and unnatural weather, continued raiding. Trading fleets from Tassato, Sarvos, the Brass Coast, Highguard and Urizen suffered reduced production.

n.Dawn: A sizable contingent of Dawnish captains joined the mapping project, and each received a copy of the map and gazetteer.
n.Grendel: The Grendel still dominate the Bay of Catazar, and their pirates raid Imperial shipping, some in the name of Siakha. Imperial mariners have now charted the shores of five Grendel territories and raided Grendel vessels and settlements along the Broken Shore.
n.Highguard: Highborn trading fleets suffered reduced production because of Grendel piracy in the Bay, and a few Highborn captains contributed to the map.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: two Imperial Orc captains are listed among the contributors to the mapping project.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: several Navarr captains are listed among the contributors to the mapping project.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn captains made up just over half the mapping expedition, and a Freeborn civil servant helped collate the results. Freeborn trading fleets also suffered reduced production from Grendel raids.
n.The League: League captains, including several from Sarvos, helped map the Bay. Trading fleets from Tassato and Sarvos suffered reduced production because of Grendel pirates.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: two Marcher captains are listed among the contributors to the mapping project.
n.Urizen: Urizeni captains helped map the Bay, but Urizeni trading fleets suffered reduced production because of Grendel piracy.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: a single Varushkan captain is listed among the contributors to the mapping project.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: several Wintermark captains are listed among the contributors to the mapping project.

t.Ayereed: The coast of this Grendel territory was mapped by Imperial captains, who found a rugged shore full of inlets and hiding places infested with pirates.
t.Bay of Catazar: The Bay's surrounding shores were charted for the Empire for the first time in detail. Grendel pirates continued to dominate its waters, and only its northern arc stayed relatively safe for Imperial ships.
t.Kalino: Imperial captains mapped the shores of this Iron Confederacy territory, where Suranni ports met them with suspicion, hold searches and sometimes refused them a berth.
t.Mareave: Imperial captains mapped the coast of this Grendel territory amid the dangers of Broken Shore pirates, using its inlets and coves to stay hidden.
t.Raineach: Imperial captains charted the shores of this Grendel territory, a rugged stretch of the Broken Shore where they could anchor briefly and explore on foot.
t.Sarvos: Trading fleets based in Sarvos suffered reduced production because of Grendel raids, and several Sarvosan captains helped map the Bay.
t.Shavronne: Imperial captains mapped the coast of this Iron Confederacy territory, where Suranni nobility treated visiting ships with suspicion and would meet defiance with force.
t.Shayeel: The shores of this Grendel territory were mapped by Imperial captains braving pirates who would enslave or sacrifice their crews.
t.Tassato: Trading fleets based in Tassato suffered reduced production because of Grendel piracy in the Bay.
t.Tathar: Imperial captains charted the coast of this Grendel territory on the Broken Shore, exploiting its islands and flooded caves to avoid orc pirates.
t.Veroigne: Imperial captains mapped this Iron Confederacy territory's shores. Robec was the exception to the generally unwelcoming Suranni ports.

Hunter of stars.d: Two horned, skull-masked heralds told the Civil Service that Capradan had not been given leave to answer. Their master, apparently not Siakha, Yaw'nagrah, Arhallogen, Irra Harah or Llofir, wanted no further messages. Adamant agreed to parley with the Summer Archmage on the Throne of Stone, the Walls of Holberg, the fortification Remember Exile and the mines of Skarsind. Ylenrith offered the Day Archmage a meeting in a chamber. Estavus offered ashes for ambergelt and talk of the lost art of the blacksmith. Sorin's heralds, through Ania of Necropolis, summoned a long list of named attendees. The Boar King agreed to meet the Night Archmage and Little Owl. Each parley was confined to agreed topics.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Sorin's message was carried by Ania of Necropolis, and Ylenrith's herald was dressed in the manner of a Highborn.
n.Imperial Orcs: The mines of Skarsind, a territory held by the Imperial Orcs, were among the four topics Adamant's representative agreed to discuss with the Summer Archmage.
n.The League: The Walls of Holberg were among the four topics Adamant agreed to discuss in formal parley, giving the League a stake in the Summer Archmage's meeting.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Ursa of Wintermark and at least two others suffering a curse from the same source were named among those Sorin's heralds expected at the parley.

t.Holberg: The Walls of Holberg were a named topic for the formal parley with Adamant's representative, and the herald was to indicate what acts would secure the boons requested.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the Draughir messenger who carried Sorin's reply was Ania of Necropolis.
t.Skarsind: The mines of Skarsind were one of four agreed topics for the parley with Adamant, whose herald would set out the acts required to secure the boons asked for.

Improve House of Barbs.d: Proposed by the senator for Semmerholm and seconded by the senator for Madruga, the motion would have upgraded the House of Barbs, a sinecure in Hercynia, so that its holder, the Voice of Barbs, gained an extra 2 liao and 4 votes in the Imperial Synod. That would have brought the sinecure to 7 liao and 14 votes each season. The work was to cost 2 wains of white granite and 4 crowns and was to be self-funded. The Senate passed the motion, but there were not enough opportunities available to commission the work, so the improvement did not go ahead.

n.Navarr: A Navarr sinecure would have grown in liao and Synod influence, but the improvement failed for lack of commission opportunities despite the Senate's approval.

t.Hercynia: The House of Barbs in Hercynia was to be enlarged with white granite to yield 7 liao and 14 votes, but the work never began because the commission failed.

Our choice.d: Bogdan Bogdanovich's mandate made clear that what affects one Varushkan army affects all. Soldiers blaming the Iron Helms for the awakening of Screed in Spiral led Wintermark and Brass Coast armies to shun every Varushkan army, cutting victory points by a tenth, or a fifth if both are present. At the Spring Equinox 382YE only, the Northern Eagle could become Plighted for 25 wains of weirwood, and the Golden Axe could become Driven for 50 wains of mithril. A consortium led by the miners of Morsvah also offered cheap enlargement of either army. Belakov Zakharovich Prochnost provided 50 mithril to make the Golden Axe Driven, and the Senate commissioned its enlargement.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish knights are recalled grumbling about the lack of glory in the historic conquest of Karsk.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel are not named; the page refers only to the Varushkan victory in Spiral, a territory they partly held.
n.Thule: In the opening fiction, a Varushkan boyar resents Thule ilium deals as chains and schemes over the star-metal brought down in Keyursal in Sküld. The page also recalls the Golden Axe crushing the Thule during the conquest of Karsk.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen are not named; the page refers only to the Varushkan victory in Spiral, a territory they partly held.
n.Varushka: Every Varushkan army now suffers penalties when campaigning with Wintermark or Brass Coast armies. The Golden Axe was set to become Driven and to be enlarged, drawing on Vard heritage and the backing of a mine- and forest-owners' consortium interested in the power of relinquishment.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark soldiers now shun Varushkan armies, believing the Iron Helms caused the awakening of Screed. Any campaign shared with a Varushkan army loses a tenth of its victory points, or a fifth if Brass Coast armies are also present.

t.Karov: Bogdan Bogdanovich spread the assembly's message here. Karov is the heartland of the Golden Axe, whose Driven transformation draws on the Vard who conquered Karov and on its wagon raiders and volhov.
t.Karsk: The miners of Morsvah in southern Karsk led the consortium offering to equip up to two and a half thousand new troops for one army. The territory's conquest under the Sun Queen is recalled as the first campaign of both the Eagle and the Axe.
t.Miekarova: Bogdan Bogdanovich carried the assembly's words here. Miekarova's Ushkan vales were a traditional recruiting ground of the Northern Eagle, which was offered the chance to become Plighted.
t.Spiral: The Varushkan victory in Spiral made many Varushkans proud. Others blamed the Iron Helms for the awakening of Screed and the madness and deaths that swept the territory, and that belief turned Wintermark and Brass Coast soldiers against Varushkan armies.
t.Volodmartz: Bogdan Bogdanovich spread the assembly's message here. Volodmartz's Ushkan vales were a traditional source of the Northern Eagle's troops.

r.Spiral/Screed: Some soldiers blame the Iron Helms' cruel tactics for the awakening of Screed and the resulting wave of madness and deaths, and that belief led to the rift with Wintermark and the Brass Coast.
r.Volodmartz/Brez: Mentioned in passing: Brez is not named; the page mentions Volodmartz only as a territory where the assembly's message spread and the Northern Eagle recruited.

Pitiless as the sun.d: Starless skies persisted over the Barrens, Zenith, Holberg and Spiral, and a strange urge to secrecy affected naga who spent time there. Penumbral veils lay over Urdur in Otkodov, Feroz, Temeschwar and Morrow, while the shrouds over Madruga and Sarvos faded. The Sussavari Frost Coven again raised a night citadel over Kallavesa, and a mysterious mist briefly wreathed Grimhold. Llofir asked to parley with the Archmage of Spring and closed Tamarbode, cutting off Tamar's Toes. Sadogua mourned Richard of Holberg. Eleonaris's herald asked for a statue marking the alliance. Meraud delayed his challenge after his hidden role in Lions of Phoenix Reach came to light. The koboldi completed the indestructible Adamant Gate in Semmerholm.

n.Dawn: Weirwater was cursed so that the name Edric de Gauvain intruded into every conversation, while Semmerholm gained the Adamant Gate, a Summer-imbued fortress that can be captured but not destroyed by normal means.
n.Druj: The Druj were said to have stolen the stars over the Barrens and Zenith and, with their forces in the heart of Screed, over Spiral too. Kaela's Gift still let their Imperial prisoners choose a painless death that left no corpse to defile.
n.Grendel: The stars over Spiral, which Grendel shared with Urizen, were devoured a week before the Equinox while the Druj occupied the heart of Screed.
n.Highguard: Highguard's region of Tamarbode in Reikos, claimed by Llofir, was closed to all Imperial citizens. The mana site of Tamar's Toes was overgrown and lost to Imperial magicians.
n.The Brass Coast: A penumbral veil, thick with dark fog, hid Feroz from scrying until shortly before the Summer Solstice, while the shroud over Madruga faded away.
n.The League: Holberg's stars stayed obscured amid fears of a hidden Druj coven, Temeschwar lay under a penumbral veil, and Sarvos's shroud faded. The League also lost its magical architect Richard of Holberg, who died of his long illness.
n.Thule: Penumbral veils hung over Urdur in Otkodov. It remained unclear whether Nithoggir, Sküld or Verthandi were veiled as well.
n.Urizen: Morrow was hidden beneath a penumbral veil, and the stars over Spiral, shared with Grendel, were devoured while the Druj held the heart of Screed.
n.Varushka: A strange mist with odd lights coiled around Grimhold Fortress in Miekarova through a lunar cycle. The Vor'Azi who live there revealed nothing of its origin.
n.Wintermark: The Sussavari Frost Coven again raised a castle of fog and shadow over Kallavesa, and Kallavesi mystics were invited to share Goosewhisper Infusion on Friday evening to seek ancestral spirits.

t.Feroz: A penumbral veil hampered scrying over Feroz and brought heavy dark fog and inky clouds. It was due to fade shortly before the Summer Solstice.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: the completion of the Wintermark beacons in Hahnmark and Kallavesa raised the question of whether Kallavesa's citadel was still needed.
t.Holberg: The stars over Holberg had been obscured since the Autumn Equinox, which raised fears of a hidden Druj coven, although no attacks had followed. Naga who spent time there felt a strong pull towards secrecy.
t.Kallavesa: A night-woven citadel raised by the Sussavari Frost Coven protected Kallavesa's lowlands until the Spring Equinox. Its future was uncertain now that the Wintermark beacons were complete.
t.Madruga: The shroud that had hung over Madruga faded away.
t.Miekarova: A serpentine mist with moving lights gathered around Grimhold Fortress through one lunar cycle, then vanished by the next new moon.
t.Morrow: A penumbral veil warped Morrow's stars to block scrying, bringing heavy fog until shortly before the Summer Solstice.
t.Otkodov: Penumbral veils hung over Urdur. Whether they also covered Otkodov's other regions could not be determined without scrying.
t.Reikos: Llofir's region of Tamarbode was sealed by armoured heralds against all mortals, ending the gathering of crystal mana at Tamar's Toes.
t.Sarvos: The shroud that had hung over Sarvos faded away.
t.Semmerholm: The koboldi of Adamant completed the Adamant Gate, a white granite fortress whose strength cannot be reduced below 1,000 and which can be captured but not destroyed by normal means.
t.Spiral: With the Druj occupying the heart of Screed, the stars over Spiral were devoured a week before the Equinox, leaving nights darker and fuller of terrors.
t.Temeschwar: A penumbral veil interfered with scrying over Temeschwar and brought dark fog until shortly before the Summer Solstice.
t.The Barrens: The stars over the Barrens remained missing, said to be stolen by the Druj. Kaela's Gift still reached Imperial captives held there.
t.Verthandi: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether the penumbral veil over Urdur also lay over Verthandi.
t.Weirwater: A curse made the name Edric de Gauvain intrude into conversation, wind and thought across Weirwater, though few knew who he was.
t.Zenith: Hopes that Zenith's stars would return before the Spring Equinox came to nothing. Kaela's Gift still extended to Imperial prisoners there.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: Some feared a hidden Druj coven lurked in Misericorde's forests beneath Holberg's starless sky, though no attacks had followed.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: The forests of Utterlund were suspected of hiding a Druj coven behind the obscured stars, but no attacks had taken place.
r.Otkodov/Nithoggir: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether the penumbral veil also covered Nithoggir.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether the penumbral veil also covered Sküld.
r.Otkodov/Urdur: Penumbral veils hung over several places in Urdur, hindering scrying there.
r.Reikos/Tamarbode: Tamarbode was sealed against all mortals by Llofir's armoured heralds. Tamar's Toes was overgrown by giant fungi and lost as a source of crystal mana.
r.Spiral/Screed: With the Druj occupying the heart of Screed, the stars above were devoured a week before the Spring Equinox.

Raise Highborn army.d: The motion, proposed by Reikos and seconded by Necropolis, called for a fourth Highborn army to be recruited in the territory of Reikos. It passed in the Senate during Spring 382YE at a cost of 0 Thrones, with standard costs applying to the army's construction. No progress had been recorded on the page, but the stated outcome was that a fourth Highborn army would be raised, adding to Highguard's military strength.

n.Highguard: Highguard was set to gain a fourth army, expanding the nation's military forces beyond its existing three Highborn armies.

t.Reikos: Reikos was chosen as the place where the new Highborn army would be recruited, and its senator proposed the motion.

Relinquish Brilliant Shore.d: Proposed by the senator for Skarsind and seconded by Sermersuaq, the motion used the Senate's power of relinquishment over the Brilliant Shore, a Bourse position in Skarsind. It passed with a constitutional majority and was ratified by the Throne, so no veto was possible. As a result, the Brilliant Shore ceased to be a National position and became available for allocation. The motion cost nothing.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs lost the Brilliant Shore as a National Bourse position in their territory of Skarsind, and control of it was opened up for allocation instead.

t.Skarsind: Skarsind's senator proposed the motion, and the Brilliant Shore on its coast stopped being a National position and became available for allocation.

Start a fire.d: The Quiet Step and its allies used Surut's fire to throw back the vallorn's push into West Ranging, but did not take the whole region. A force unlike anything seen before seems to be at work in Liathaven. Retaking the ancient Westwood is a far riskier prospect, and it must happen by the Winter Solstice. Several options were offered. The Synod could pass mandates urging soldiers to fight in Liathaven. Surut offered more boons in return for Conclave amity. Brokers proposed a ministry in Miaren supplying anti-vallorn tools. The Dance of Navarr and Thorn had already restored trods in Mournwold and around Liathaven, leaving only Spiral's trods broken.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj withdrawal left the empty space the vallorn spread into, and Zenith is said to have fallen to them.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: a soldier refers to rumours of a massacre in Spiral.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: a Marcher soldier has heard there are Jotun in Wintermark.
n.Navarr: The Quiet Step won a costly victory, and the Navarr assembly could bind its thorns to the Liathaven fight by mandate. Navarr brokers and vates were weighing a Miaren ministry and help from Surut or Arhallogen.
n.The Marches: Marcher troops fought beside the Navarr to burn out the vallorn in Liathaven. The trods in the Marcher-held Mournwold were repaired during the Winter Solstice.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: a soldier predicts war with the Thule again soon.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: listed among the Empire's ongoing wars.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Marchers talk of marching north to Sermersuaq against the Jotun.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: its earlier vallorn expansion is compared with Liathaven's, and the restored trods now encircle its vallorn.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: the trods now wrap around its vallorn.
t.Liathaven: The vallorn here was beaten back and weakened, and a mysterious new power seems to be stirring. The Westwood could be reclaimed if enough force arrives before the Winter Solstice.
t.Miaren: Navarr brokers gathered here and proposed building a brokerage to supply roseweald, bladeroot, Oil of Blackroot and Scorpion's Sting daggers. It could only be built at the Spring Equinox.
t.Mournwold: The Dance of Navarr and Thorn reinforced and repaired trods here that had suffered thirty years or more of neglect.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Marchers speculate about marching north to Sermersuaq.
t.Spiral: It is the only territory where the trods remain broken and fading. Most vates believe they could be rewoven from the Anvil regio despite the plateau's dark influence.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the trods now wrap around its vallorn.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: a soldier says Zenith has gone to the Druj.

r.Brocéliande/Elerael: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns thwarted a similar vallorn expansion here a few years earlier.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: The vallorn's push here was driven back by Surut's fire, but the Empire does not control the whole region. Securing it would spare an attack on Westwood the penalties of a beachhead.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: This ancient heart of the vallorn, untouched for over a thousand years, could be reclaimed by a well-supported attack before the Winter Solstice. Divination is needed first to gauge its strength.

The whole world.d: Liao rose to 18 rings a dose. Magician-Prince Barbara Radz of Rigia was killed in a coup, the port closed and the Imperial embassy damaged. Sumaah sent a delegation to Anvil under a ceasefire. Nemoria stopped selling herbs and now pays money instead. The architect Almodin Oktístis offered a third seasonal commission in return for a temple to Baddu, but threatened to quit if another of his works was defiled. Faraden declined a theological exchange. Axos offered staged abolition of slavery if trade was sustained. Robec opened to Imperial captains. With Zenith taken by the Druj, the Sarcophan offered cheap white granite, the Axou a deadly fortification design and the Jarmish faster construction to protect Cargo.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Astolat is named as one of the preferred sites for a proposed Asavean temple of Baddu the Builder.
n.Druj: Having conquered Zenith, the Druj now threaten Limus and Cargo, and the embassies there are urgently seeking ways to defend the town against them.
n.Grendel: Grendel traders are offering cheap slaves to patrons in Issyk to undermine the Imperial push for abolition in Axos, and their pact with the Sarcophan keeps Sarcophan ships unmolested.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is a preferred site for the proposed temple of Baddu, and the Chantry of the Silver Skull is listed among the places of religious learning.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Seminary of the Hall of the White Ravens and the Legion's Rookery in Skarsind are listed as places for religious debate with Faraden priests.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Faraden merchants transported mithril through Jotun lands, at some expense, for auction through the Bourse.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is named as a preferred site for the proposed Asavean temple of Baddu.
n.The Brass Coast: Work has begun on extending the Blood Red Roads from Anduz in Segura to Madruga, the Iron Confederacy has opened Robec after developments in Feroz, and the Commonwealth ambassador in Siroc has made statements of interest to the Freeborn.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the School of Epistemology is listed as a place of religious learning, and Temeschwar is a preferred site for the proposed temple of Baddu.
n.The Marches: The completed Faraden trading enclave, Moonwater Hall in Upwold, is bringing prosperity to the Marches and drawing more Faraden merchants into the Empire.
n.Urizen: Urizen has lost Zenith to the Druj, and Cargo in Redoubt, with its embassies, docks and nearby runeforge, is now at risk unless the Senate fortifies it with foreign help.
n.Varushka: The architect Almodin Oktístis was enraged that his fortification in Karsk, Aleksandra's Watch, had been defiled, and he warned that any repeat would make him leave the Empire.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Meagenstede Hall is listed among the places of learning for religious debate with Faraden priests.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Astolat is one of the preferred central locations for the proposed temple of Baddu the Builder.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Sarcophan ships regularly visit ports along the Bay, where their pact with the Grendel causes some discontent.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is one of the preferred central locations for the proposed temple of Baddu the Builder.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: developments in Feroz are cited alongside improving relations with the Iron Confederacy.
t.Karsk: Aleksandra's Watch in Karsk was "defiled by philistines" with Senate approval, which nearly drove its architect Almodin Oktístis to quit the Empire.
t.Madruga: Work has begun on extending the Blood Red Roads to Madruga, which will give Faraden merchants easy access across the Empire.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is one of the preferred central locations for the proposed temple of Baddu the Builder.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the new runeforge lies a short walk from Cargo along the road towards Necropolis.
t.Redoubt: Cargo in Redoubt is threatened by the Druj, and the Sarcophan, Axou and Jarmish embassies there have each offered help if the Senate commissions a fortification for the town.
t.Segura: Work has begun on extending the Blood Red Roads from Anduz in Segura to Madruga, and the Towers of Anduz are listed as a place of religious learning.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: two places of learning in Skarsind are listed for religious debate with Faraden priests.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar is one of the preferred central locations for the proposed temple of Baddu the Builder.
t.Upwold: The completion of the Faraden enclave Moonwater Hall has brought prosperity to Upwold.
t.Zenith: Zenith has been conquered by the Druj, who have destroyed the settlements they captured there.

r.Redoubt/Limus: Limus is the likely starting point of any Druj assault on Redoubt, putting Cargo's embassies, the Concordium and Pallas Docks and the nearby runeforge at risk, and prompting foreign offers to help fortify Cargo.

United in law.d: Delivered through the Throne's power to address the Empire, Lisabetta reminded citizens that their oath binds them to support the law, and that Clemency requires other legal avenues to be pursued first. She mourned Senator Gant Archama of Temeschwar, who died defending Zenith against the Druj, and condemned the murder of Senator Lady Jocelyn Cordraco and the lawless killing and execution that followed. She pledged greater support for the citizen Militia, praising Nadia Borodina di Sarvos. Following League tradition, she announced she would seek a spouse, negotiated by Benedict Pacelli von Holberg. Finally, with the Mournwold reclaimed, she granted Sarcombe an Imperial Charter to encourage rebuilding and trade.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the address names the "reviled Druj" as the enemy against whom Senator Gant Archama died defending Zenith.
n.The League: The Imperatrix invoked League tradition of marrying at the height of one's power, entrusting her marriage negotiations to the Master of Hearts of the House of Seven Mirrors, and mourned Senator Gant Archama of Temeschwar.
n.The Marches: With the Mournwold reclaimed, the Throne granted an Imperial Charter to Sarcombe, seeking to restore trade between the people of the Mourn and the rest of the Empire.

t.Mournwold: The address celebrated the reclamation of the Mournwold and the chance to restore its commerce with the wider Empire through Sarcombe's charter.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Senator Gant Archama of Temeschwar was honoured for giving his life defending Zenith at the Winter 381YE summit.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Imperatrix grieved the failed defence of Zenith against the Druj, in which Senator Gant Archama and many others died.

r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Sarcombe in Southmoor, already legally restored as a market town by the Senate, received an Imperial Charter to encourage further rebuilding and prosperous trade.

You'll recognise yourself.d: Supporters argued the Senate lacked ambition and time, and proposed a Master of Commissions title for la Volpe, subject to the Imperatrix's veto. Detractors, many from Highguard, called his works gauche and also condemned an Asavean architect's blasphemous works. They proposed a constitutional motion moving commissions to the Synod, an idea the constitutional court deemed constitutional in principle. Projects seeking his money were a dam in Madruga, cold-store caverns in Volodmartz, a pig farm at Graven, a taller Colossus near Tassato, a Therunin smithy and Holberg sausage distribution. Projects rejecting him were pilgrim hostels for Bastion, a Laroc arena (later superseded) and the Bleak Tower arboretum in Morrow. The opportunities remained open until the end of the Summer Solstice.

n.Dawn: Lady Larille de Rochemont proposed a magnificent new tournament arena at Laroc, appealing to two noble houses for support. It would aid Astolat's troubadours and let Dawn raise armies there faster, though this opportunity was later superseded.
n.Druj: The Druj invasion of Zenith had destroyed the Gardens of Pallas, scattering Urizeni herbalists as refugees into Morrow. Their past siege of Holberg was also recalled.
n.Highguard: Much of the opposition to la Volpe and the Asavean architect came from Highguard. Philemon of Fulmon's Bounty proposed pilgrim hostels for Bastion and refused any of la Volpe's money.
n.Navarr: The broker Cyfarth proposed a great cleaver-walled smithy in Peakedge Song to enrich Therunin's mines. Supporters of la Volpe derided the Navarr Dredgemaster of Feverwater as an indulgent sinecure.
n.The Brass Coast: The Galia family of Madruga sought la Volpe's backing for a great irrigation dam bearing the Butchers' symbols, which would yield a water-contract sinecure.
n.The League: La Volpe's growing fame was centred on the League, where Tassato residents proposed a taller rival Colossus and Holberg's Virtuous Company sought to spread Holberg sausage across the Empire under the Butchers' brand.
n.The Marches: The alders of Graven proposed a vast Blood Red Pig Farm to improve their bargaining position with local yeofolk, offering la Volpe an honorary citizenship if he funded it.
n.Urizen: Cyrus of the White Stair proposed restoring Morrow's Bleak Tower as an arboretum for refugee herbalists from Zenith. He sought Achilles of Damakan's Forge as benefactor rather than la Volpe.
n.Varushka: Boyar Petra of the Vale of Stars proposed fortifying the cold Star Caverns in Volodmartz as a food and herb store, extending his vale's protection over them.

t.Astolat: A grand new arena at Laroc was proposed, which would bring liao and votes to Astolat's congregations and quicken the raising of Dawnish armies there. This opportunity was later superseded.
t.Bastion: Pilgrim hostels along the hoped-for Blood Red Roads were proposed, which would bring liao and Synod votes to Bastion's congregations. They would yield only half their benefit unless the roads reached the city.
t.Bregasland: Graven, Bregasland's largest town, proposed a huge pig farm and abattoir. It would supply the town and its miners and give its overseer access to weltsilver and green iron.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the Galia farms' grain and salted pork were unloaded weekly in Siroc.
t.Holberg: The Virtuous Company of Provisioners proposed expanding distribution of Holberg rations, bringing a bounty to every farm in Holberg. Rival food sellers accused them of seeking a monopoly.
t.Madruga: The Galia family proposed a great dam creating an artificial lake to irrigate their dry farms upriver from Lightsea.
t.Morrow: The ruined Bleak Tower, with its winter regio, was proposed for restoration as an arboretum. It would boost Morrow's herb gardens and give a custodian rare Heart's Blood each season.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos's Colossus was mocked by detractors. A rival statue near Tassato would cost the city some of the income its Colossus generated.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: la Volpe had once announced plans to extend the Blood Red Roads as far as Anduz in Segura.
t.Tassato: Residents proposed a larger, partly hollow Colossus of la Volpe on the Red Rock overlooking the Sapphire Stair. It would bring extra income to Tassato's businesses.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: la Volpe is the Merchant Prince of Temeschwar, whose fame drove these proposals.
t.Therunin: A great smithy was proposed in Peakedge Song that would generate a bounty spread among all Therunin's mines.
t.Volodmartz: A plan to deepen and fortify the legendary Star Caverns in Marupa was proposed. The caverns would store food and herbs, and their overseer could buy bladeroot.
t.Zenith: Following the Druj conquest of Zenith, the Gardens of Pallas were destroyed and their herbalists fled as refugees to Morrow.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: The town of Graven proposed building the Blood Red Pig Farm on its northern edge to feed the town and supply its miners.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: The proposed Galia dam would lie thirty miles upriver from the coast at Lightsea, securing water for the family's farms.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: Cyfarth's proposed great smithy would stand on Peakedge Song's stable, mine-rich ground. Its walls could be carved as cleavers in la Volpe's honour.
r.Zenith/Iteri: The Druj had flooded the Gardens of Pallas in central Iteri, smashed their ushabti and burned their caretaker spires.
